hymns.title: Oh! timely happy, timely wise
verses:
Oh! timely happy, timely wise,
Hearts that with rising morn arise!
Eyes that the beam celestial view,
Which evermore makes all things new!
New every morning js the love
Our wakening and uprising prove,
Through sleep and darkness safely

brought, p Only, O Lord, in Thy dear love,
Restored to life, and power, and thought.
New mercies each returning day,
Hover around us while we pray

New perils past, new sins forgiven.
New thoughts of God, new hopes of

If on our daily course our mind
Be set to hallow all we find,
New treasures still, of countless price,
God will provide fur sacrifice.

Fit as for perfect rest above
And help us, this and every day,
To live more nearly a3 we pray.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O splendour of the Father's beam
verses:
O splendour of the Father's beam,
Who draw'st from Light its faintest ray
Thyself the Fount of every gleam
ay-star, that givest light to day.

True Sun of Righteousness arise
In sheen of ever-streaming light,
Outpour Thy Spirit from the skies,
On mortal sense a radiance bright.

O Father, come to help our vows,
Thou Father of Almighty Grace
Eternal glory crowns Thy brows
Each guileful sin do Thou erase,

Direct and rule the erring soul,
May Chastity unspotted reign!
Faith burn with fervour's living coal,
Unknowing craft's insidious bane!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Christ, Whose glory fills the skies
verses:
Christ, Whose glory fills the skies,
Christ, the true, the only Light,
Sun of Righteousness, arise,
Triumph o'er the shades of night!
Day-spring from on high, be near
Day-star, in my heart appear!

Dark and cheerless is the morn,
Unaccompanied by Thee
Joyless is the day's return,
Till Thy mercy's beams I see:
Till they inward light impart,
Glad my eyes, and warm my heart,

Visit then this soul of mine,
Pierce the gloom of sin and grief!
eres, Fill me, Radiancy divine
Scatter all my unbelief!
More and more Thyself display,
Shining to the perfect day!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: This morning light hath shed its beams
verses:
This morning light hath shed its beams,
And paved its way in living streams:
Rise. Christian! meet the ray!
my And while it pours its golden fire,
Oh, let it golden thoughts inspire:
Up, Christian. hail the dzy!

Then when the day draws near the West,
And tells thee of approaching rest,
To exse thy weary head.
O pray a Saviour's richest love
May drop in radiance from above,
To gild thy dying bed

my For Satan comes in light's array,
To haunt us lest we kneel and pray:
Quick! humbly Currst adore t t
That He may rise thy leading star,
To warm and licht thee from afar,
Thy brightness evermore.

If night hath dropped a spot of bane
To soil thy conscience. wash the stain

Fall st-eng: bened by His cordisl Graea,
Essay thy :oul's diarnal race,
Sustained by saintly food.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Look forth, mine eye, look up, and view
verses:
Look forth, mine eye, look up, and view,
How bright the daylight shines on me;
And as the morning doth renew,
Mark how renewed God's mercies be.

Behold the splendors of the day
Disperse the shadows of the night;
And they, who late in darkness lay,
Ifave now the comforts of the light.

So when that morning doth appear,
In which Thou shalt all flesh destroy,
We shall not be awaked with fear,
But rise and mect Thy Son with joy.

Nor twilight plagues, nor midnight fears,
Nor mortal, nor immortal foes,
Had power to take us in their snares,
But safe we slept, and safe arose.

Let heart, and hand, and voice accord
This day to magnify Thy Name
And let us every day, O Lord!
Continue to perform the same.

To shield us from the shafts of 'iM,
While we our daily tasks fulfil.
The tongue of license may He curb,
Lest strife should sweet repose disturb;
And may He softly screen the sight,
Lest it should drink of vain delight.
Our inmost thoughts be ever pure!
May sinful folly ne'er allure!

That when the daylight disappears,
And night again her shade uprears,
We, saved from every worldly stain,
To God may lift the thankful strain.
F To God the Father give the praise,
To God the Son the same upraise
With Both the Comrorter adore,
From age to age, for evermore.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O God of morning, at Whose voice
verses:
O God of morning, at Whose voice
The cheerful sun makes haste to rise,
And like a giant doth rejoice
To run his journey through the skies;

From fairest chambers of the East
The circuit of his race begins
Withont or weariness or rest,
Around the earth he flies and shines:

Oh! like the sun may I fulfil
Th' appointed duties of the day:
With ready mind, and active wil},
March on, and keep my heav'nly way!

But IJ shall rove, and lose the race,
If God, my Sun, shall disappear,
And leave me in this world's wild maze,
To follow every wandering star.

Thy counsel give me for my guide,
id then receive me to Thy bliss:
All my desires and hopes beside
Are faint and cold compared with this.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Rise, my soul, adore thy Maker
verses:
Rise, my soul, adore thy Maker!
Angels praise
Join thy lays;
'With them be partaker.

FatTuHER, Lord of every spirit,
In Thy light,
Lead me right,
Through my Sayiour's merit.

Never cast me from Thy Presence
Till my soul
Shall be full
Of Thy blessed Essence.

O Lord Jesus, Gov Almighty,
Pray for me
Till I see
Thee in Salem's city.

Hoty Guost, by JEsus given,
Be my Guide
Lest my pride
Shut me out of heaven.

Thou the night wast my Protector:
With me stay
All the day,
Ever my Director.

Holy, holy, holy Giver
all good,
Life and food,
Reign, adored for ever!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: All praise to Thee, my God, this night
verses:
All praise to Thee, my God, this night,
For all the blessings of the light,
Keep me, O keep me, Krve of Kings,
Beneath Thine Own Almighty wings.

Forgive me, Lord, for Thy dear Son,
The ill that I this day have done;
That with the world, myself, and Thee,
I, ereI sleep, at peace may be.

Teach me to live, that I may dread
The grave as little as my bed!
To die, that this vile body may
Rise glorious at the awful Day.

O may my soul on Thee repose,
d may sweet sleep mine eyelids close
Sleep, that may me more vig'rous make
To serve my God when I awake!

When in the night I sleepless lie,
My soul with heavenly thoughts supply!
Let no ill dreams disturb my rest,
No powers of darkness me molest!

Praise God, from Whom all blessings flow
Praise Him, all creatures here below!
Praise Him above, ye heavenly host!
Praise Father, Son, and Hoty Guost!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Sun of my soul, Thou Saviour dear
verses:
Sun of my soul, Thou Saviour dear,
It is not night if Thou be near:
O may no earth-born cloud arise
To hide Thee from Thy servant's eyes.

When the soft dews of kindly sleep
My wearied eyelids gently steep,
Be my last thought how sweet to rest
For ever on my Saviour's breast.

A | bide with | me from morn till eve,
For without hee I cannot live;
A | bide with | me when night is nigh,
For without Thee I dare not die.

If some poor wand''ring child of Thine
Iiave spurned to-day the voice divine,
Now, Lord, the gracious work begin;
Let him no more lie down in sin.

Watch by the sick; enrich the poor
With blessings from Thy boundless store;
Be every mourner's sleep to-night,
Like infants' slumbers, pure and light.

Come near and bless us when we wake.
Ere through the world our way we take,
Till in the ocean of Thy love
We lose ourselves in heaven above.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Now the shining day is past
verses:
Now the shining day is past,
And the beauties of the light
Are with shadows overcast
By the mantle of the night:
Thanks to Thee, O Lord, I pay
For the blessings of this day;
Asking grace for every sin,
Whereby erred I have therein.

Though the Sun hath left us now,
And withholds his light from me;
Lord, from hence depart not Thou,
Nor in darkness let me be;
But the rays of Grace divine
Cause Thou round me still to shine,
And with mercy overspread
Both my person and my bed.

my Chase all wicked fiends from hence,
That they do me no despite,
By deluding of the sense
Through the darkness of the night;
But, O Lord, from all my foes
Let Thine angels me inclose,
And protect me in my sleep,
When myself I cannot keep.

And since death and sleep are said
Some resemblances to have,
In my bed ere I am laid
So prepare me for my grave,
That with comfort wake I may,
To enjoy the following day;
Or if death close up mine eyes,
Rest in hope till all shall rise.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Abide with me; fast falls the eventide
verses:
Abide with me; fast falls the eventide
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide!
When other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life's little day
Earth's joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see,
O Thou, Who changest not, abide with me.

I need Thy Presence every passing hour;
What but Thy Grace can foil the Tempter's power
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be
Through cloud and sunshine O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless;
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness:
Where is Death's sting ? where, Grave, thy victory
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me,

Hold Thou Thy Cross before my closing eyes!
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies!
Heaven's morning breaks, and earth's vain shadows flee;
In life and death, O Lord, abide with me!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The Christian's path shines more and more
verses:
When comforts fail, and friends are few,
And griefs his path surround
Though all is dark without, within,
A heav'nly light is found;
No change of scene his peace can blight,
At evening time it shall be light.

*Tis good at times that pilgrim saints
For but a moment's space,
Should feel that God, in wrath at sin,
Can hide His smiling face:
Behind that veil the sun shines bright,
At evening time it shall be light.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord, ever shew Thy blessed face
verses:
Lord, ever shew Thy blessed face,
Though downward sinks the sun;
Stand still in heav'n, with looks of grace,
Though he his course hath run:
Above the height,
In glory bright,
Still shines in Thee unfading light.

As speeds the moon her silent way,
Outpouring softest beams
So shed on us a gentle ray,
To silver o'er our dreams;
With thoughts snow-white,
To hallow night,
Illumined by Thy purest light.

When calmly laid in quiet rest,
Sweet slumber on our eyes,
Let angels hover round each breast,
Our guard till morning rise:
Sin takes to flight,
And drops the fight;
For Thou art peace as well as light.

Thus screened from danger, safe from harm,
We live Thine Own by day
Still Thine, enfolded in Thine Arm,
While darkness beareth sway
Thyself, blest Sight,
peal day and night,
to us in radiant light,

As sighs our last departing breath,
And friends in sorrow weep,
Oh! grant us, Lord, a tranquil death,
Like this, a restful sleep
res. Then, through Thy might,
Raise us all bright,
Toview Thee robed in quenchless light!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Ere I sleep, for every favour
verses:
Ere I sleep, for every favour,
This day shewed
By my God,
I will bless my Savior.

O my Lord, what shall I render
'o Thy Name,
Still the same,
Gracious, good, and tender?

Thou hast ordered all my goings
In Thy way:
Hear me pray,
Sanctify my doings.

So, whene'er in death I slumber,
creés. Let me rise
With the wise,
JF Counted in their number.

Leave me not, but ever love me;
Let Thy peace
Be my bliss,
Till Thou hence remove me.

Visit me with Thy salvation
Let Thy care
Now be near,
Round my habitation.

Thou, my Rock, my Guard, my Tower,
Safely keep
While I sleep,
Me with all Thy power
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Saviour, breathe an evening blessing
verses:
Saviour, breathe an evening blessing,
Ere repose our spirits seal
Sin and want we come confessing:
Thou canst save, and Thou canst

Though destruction walk around us,
Though the arrow past us fly,
Angel-guards from Thee surround us
We are safe if Thou art nigh.

Though the night be dark and dreary,
Darkness cannot hide from Thee;
Thou art He, Who, never weary,
Watchest where Thy people be.

Should swift death this night o'er-
take us,
And our couch become our tomb,
May the morn in heaven awake us,
Clad in light and deathless bloom!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Haz my prayer, O Heavenly Father
verses:
Haz my prayer, O Heavenly Father,
Ere I lay me down to sleep:
Bid Thy Angels, pure and holy,
Round my bed their vigil keep.

Heavy though my sins, Thy mercy
Far outweighs them every one;
Down before Thy Cross I cast them,
Trusting in Thy help alone.

Pardon all my past transgressions
Give me strength for days to come;
Guide and guard me with Thy blessing,
Till Thine angels bid me home

Keep me, through this night of peril,
Underneath its boundless shade
Take me to Thy rest, I pray Thee,
When my pilgrimage is made.

None shall measure out Thy patience
By the space of human thought
None shall bound the tender mercies
Which Thy Holy Son hath bought.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: To Thy temple I repair
verses:
To Thy temple I repair
Lord, I love to worship there;
When, within the veil, I meet
Christ before the mercy-seat

Thou, through Him, art reconciled
I, through Him, become Thy child
Abba, Father, give me grace
In Thy courts to seek Thy face!

While Thy glorious praise is sung,
Touch my lips, unloose my tongue,
That my joyful soul may bless
Thee, the Lord our Righteousness

While the prayers of saints ascend.
God of Love, to mine attend!
Hear me, for Thy Spirit pleads;
Hear, for Jesus intercedes.

While I hearken to Thy law,
Fill my soul with huntble aw
Till Thy Gospel bring to me
Life and immortality.

From Thy house when I return
May my heart within me burn,
And at evening let me say:
IT have walked with God to-day
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: On each return of holy rest
verses:
On each return of holy rest,
The day my heavenly FatueEr blest,
O let my happy portion be
To find supreme delight in Thee
JS In Thee, my God, in Thee!

When, humbly kneeling at Thy Throne,
With deep distress my guilt I own,
Then let my contrite spirit see
Enough of pardoning grace in Thee;
In Thee, my God, in Thee!

When in Thy temple I adore,
And Truth's unfathomed mines explore : F
Or trembling praise the One in Three,
Fresh glories let me view in Thee;
In Thee, my God, in Thee!

Thus, on each day of holy rest,
May I with heavenly joy be blest,
And, in a bright eternity,
Have my undying bliss in Thee;
In Thee, my God, in Thee!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The Krxce Himself comes near
verses:
The Krxce Himself comes near,
And feasts Ilis saints to-day
We here may sit, and see Him here.
And love, and praise, and pray.

My willing soul would stay
In such a frame as this,
And sit, and sing herself away
To everlasting bliss.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: May Charity, with ardent glow
verses:
May Charity, with ardent glow,
Qn every heart profusely flow,
While we with voice triumphant sing
High praise to our life-giving Kine.
O Faruer, Who hast fixed on me
The stamp of Thy Divinity,

Be Thou a torch of quenchless light!
Inflame my breast to seek Thy sight!
O Sovereren of my heart, to Thee,
Thrice holy, do I bend my knee;
Thine ever through each passing hour,
I love Thee with my utmost power.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Lord of holy Rest, we pray
verses:
O Lord of holy Rest, we pray
In this Thy house. on this Thy day!
Own Thou, as grateful sacrifice,
The songs which from our lips arise.

Thine earthly Sabbaths, Lord, we love;
But there's a nobler rest above:
To that our lab'ring souls aspire,
With ardent pangs of strong desire,

No more fatigue, no more distress
Nor sin, nor hell shall reach the place q
No groans to mingle with the songs,
Which warble from immortal tongues,

No rude alarms of raging foes
No cares to break the long repose;
No midnight shade, no clouded sun,
But sacred, high, eternal noon.

O long-expected day, begin!
Rise o'er these realms of woe and sin!
dim, We fain would leave this wea road,
And sleep in death, to rest with God.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The first and best of days
verses:
The first and best of days:
The toiler's rest, the saint's delight,
A day of joy and praise:
My Saviour's face did make thee
shine, Are these sweet feasts of love;
His rising thee did raise;
This made thee heavenly and divine
Beyond all other days.

The first-fruits do a blessing prove
To all the sheaves behind;
And they, that do a Sabbath love,
A happy week shall find:
My LoxpD on thee His Name did fix,
Which makes thee rich and gay;
Amidst His golden candlesticks
My Saviour walks this day.

Mak'st them a weekly feast;
Thy flocks assemble in Thy folds
On this Thy day of rest.
Right dear and welcome to my soul

But what a Sabbath shall I keep,
When I shall rest above!

This day must I for God appear
For, Lord, this day is Thine:
Oh, let me spend it in Thy fear!
The day shall then be mine.
It is my preparation-day
And when my soul is drest,
These Sabbaths shall deliver me
To mine eternal rest.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Jesus calls us 'mid the tumalt
verses:
Jesus calls us 'mid the tumalt,
Reigning o'er life's troubled sea
Ever sweet His voice resoundeth,
Saying, “ Christian, follow Me.”

As of old St. Andrew heard it
By the Galilean lake,
Turned from home, and toil, and kindred,
Leaving all for His dear sake.

Jesus calls us: by Thy mercies,
Saviour, may we hear Thy call
Give our hearts to Thy obedience,
Serve and love Thee best of all!

Jesus calls us from the worship,
Paid to lucre's golden store
Luring us from every idol,
Saying, “ Christian, love Me more.”

'Midst our joys, and pains, and sorrows,
Days of toil, and hours of ease,
Still He calls, in cares and pleasures,
“Christian, love Me more than these.”
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Hark! a trumpet voice of warning
verses:
Hark! a trumpet voice of warning
Pealeth through the realms of Night:
“Chase afar the dreams of darkness;
Christ descends in flames of light."

Let the soul shake off her torpor,
Bound no more to mortal clay
Bursts the Morning-Star in brightness,
Quenching every banefal ray.

Might and honor, praise and glory,
Give the Father and the Son;
Join the Spier in the homage,
Long as endless ages run.

Lo! the Lams, with free remission,
Guilt to cancel, quits His seat:
Sinners! haste with tearful sorrow
His forgiving Grace entreat.

Then. when next He beams in splendor,
Girding round the world with dread,
He above His ransomed people
Shall a shield of mercy spread.

THE Lord of might, from Sinai's brow,
Gave forth His voice of thunder
And Israel lay on earth below,
Outstretched in fear and wonder:
Beneath His feet was pitchy night.
And at His left hand, and His right,
The rocks were rent in sunder.

The Lord of Love, on Calvary,
A meek and suffering stranger,
Upraised to heaven His languid eye,
In Nature's hour of danger:
For us He bore the weight of woe,
For us He gave His Blood to flow,
And met His Father's anger.

The Lord of Love, the Lord of Might.
The Kine of all created,
Shall back return to claim His right,
On clouds of glory seated
With trumpet-sound, and angel-song
And hallelujahs leud and long,
O'cr death and hell defeated.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Blest Framer of the starry height
verses:
Blest Framer of the starry height,
Believers' everlasting Light,
Good Jesu, Saviorr of us all,
O listen as we humbly call.

Lest Earth, betrayed by wiles of Hell,
Should perish, Thou hast broke the spell;
And, fired by love, unfailing, sure,
For sin-sick man art found the cure.

To blot away that common sin,
Which stained the world without, within,
Thou, Cross-ward, from the Virgin's shrine,
Art hasting, spotless Laws, divine.

When once Thy Name, in glorious power,
Comes ringing on the midnight hour,
The stooping hosts of Heaven and Hel:
With trembling knee their terror tell.

Avert Thy anger, Thee we pray.
Great Judge of that last, awful Day,
With weapons of Thy heavenly Grace,
O screen us from the foeman's face.

7 Might, honour, majesty, and praise,
To God the Father high we raise;
With God the Srinit laud the Son,
Till rolling ages cease to run.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lo! He comes with clouds descending
verses:
Lo! He comes with clouds descending,
Once for favoured sinners slain;
Thousand thousand saints attending
Swell the triumph of His train:

Every eye shall now behold Him,
Robed in dreadful majesty
Tho-e, who set at nought and sold Him,
Pierced. and nailed Him to the tree,
Deeply wailing,
Shall the true MEssiag see.

Those dear tokens of His Passion
Still His dazzling Body bears,
Cause of endless exultation
To His ransomed worshippers
With what rapture
Gaze we on those glorious scars!

Yea, Amen, let all adore Thee!
High on Thine eternal Throne!
Saviovr, take the power and glory,
Claim the Kingdom for Thine Own:
O come quickly!
Everlasting God, come down!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Great God, what do I see and hear
verses:
Great God, what do I see and hear!
The end of things created!
The Judge of mankind doth appear.
On clouds of glory seated!
The trumpet sounds! the graves restore
The dead, which they contained before
Prepare, my soul, to meet him!

The dead in Christ are first to rise,
And greet th' Archangel's warning,
To meet the Saviour in the skies
On this tremendous morning:

But sinners, filled with guilty fears,
Behold His wrath prevailing
In woe they rise, and find their tears
And sighs are unavailing:
The day of Grace is past and gone
They trembling stand before the Throne,
All unprepared to meet Him.

But let not dread my bosom wring,
A load of horror bearing
A wondrous sight doth comfort bring:
_ The Judge my nature wearing!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Hark! hark the sound! the Saviour comes
verses:
Hark! hark the sound! the Saviour comes,
The Saviovg, promised long;
Let every heart prepdre a throne,
And every voice a song!

He comes, the prisoners to release,
In Satan's bondage held
The gates of brass before Him burst,
The iron fetters yield.

He comes, the broken heart to bind,
The bleeding soul to cure,
And with the treasures of His Grace
T' enrich the humble poor.

Our glad Hosannas, Prince of PEacr,
Thy welcome shall proclaim,
And Heav'n's eternal arches ring
With Thy beloved Name.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O come, EmMaNcr, O come
verses:
O come, EmMaNcr, O come!
Thy captive ransom from her doom!
In exile Israel doth mourn,
Of Thee, the Son of God, forlorn.
Rejoice! rejoice! Emmancer
Is born for thee, O Israe]!

Come, Rod of Jesse! Save Thine Own,
Beneath the feet of Satan thrown!
O snatch them from the pit of Hell.
And break the Tempter's darkest spell!
Rejoice! rejoice! EmManveL
Is born for thee, O Israel!

O come, O come, great Lord of might!
Who once, from Sinai's flaming height,
Didst give the universe Thy law,
"Mid glory, majesty, and awe!

O bring us comfort from afar!
Disperse the darkling clouds of night,

Rejoice! rejoice! Exotance.

Come, Key of David! speed Thy way!
Unlock the realms of heavenly day!
Celestial paths of safety show,
And close each road to Hell below
Rejoice! rejoice! ExnranveL
Is born for thee, O Is:ael!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lo! He comes! Let all adore Him
verses:
Lo! He comes! Let all adore Him!
*Tis the God of grace and truth!
Go! prepare the way before Him!
Make the rugged places smooth!
Lo! He comes, the mighty Lord!
Great His work, and His reward.

Where the thorn and briar flourishcd,
'Trees shall there be seen to grow,
Planted by the Lord, and nourished,
Stately, fair, and fruitful too:
They shall rise on every side;
They shall spread their branches wide.

Down the hills, and lofty mountains,
Rivers shall be seen to flow
There the Lord will open fountains,
Thence supply the plains below:
As He passes, every land
Shall confess His powerful hand.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Txovu Judge of quick and dead
verses:
Txovu Judge of quick and dead,
Before whose bar severe,
With holy joy, or guilty dread,
We all shall soon appear;
Our souls do Thou prepare
For that tremendous day,
And fill us now with watchful care,
And stir us up to pray;

To pray, and wait the hour,
That awful hour unknown,
When, robed in majesty and pow'r,
Thou shalt from heaven come down,
Th' immortal Son of Man,
To judge the human race,
With all T h Father's dazzling train,
With a! cf Thy glorious grace.

To damp our earthly joys,
T' increase our holy fears,
For ever let th' Archangel's voice
Be sounding in our ears
The solemn midnight cry:
Ye dead, the Judge is come:
Arise, and meet Him in the sky,
And meet your instant doom!"

Oh! may we all be found
Obedient to Thy word,
Attentive to the trumpet's sound,
And looking for our Lord!
Oh! may we thus insure
A lot among the blest,
And watch a moment, to secure
An everlasting rest!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Day of Judgment! Day of wonders
verses:
Day of Judgment! Day of wonders!
Hark! the trumpet's awful sound
Louder than a thousand thunders,
Shakes the vast creation round!
How the summons
Will the sinner's heart confound

See the Judge, our nature wearing,
Clothed in majesty divine!
You, who long for His appearin
Then shall say, '' This God is mine!”
Gracious SAvrourR,
Own me in that day for Thine!

At His eall the dead awaken,
Rise to life from earth and sea;
All the pow'rs of Nature, shaken
By His looks, prepare to flee
Careless sinner,
What will then become of thee

But to those, who have confesséd,
Loved and served the Lord below,
He will say, '' Come near, ye blessed,
See the kingdom I bestow:
You, for ever,
Shall My love and glory know.”

Under sorrows and reproaches
May this thought our courage raise!
Swiftly God's Great Day approaches ; 8
Sighs shall then be turned to praise:
We shall triumph
When the world is in a blaze!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O par of wrath! that awful Day
verses:
O par of wrath! that awful Day!
In ashes earth shall melt away!
A wreck that kindled David's lay.
How dread the thrill shall shake her floor,
When He, the Judge, shall near the door,
With rigour all things to explore!

JF The trump shall send its wondrous sound
Throughout the graves, that line the ground,
To muster to the Throne around
Their tenants, rising through the vast,
As Death and Nature look aghast,
To answer to the Judge at last.

my The Book of Record shall be spread,
Wherein the swollen list is read,
From which shall earth's arraign be sped.
Then when He seats Himself in Light,
Each secret shall be torn from Night
Nought unavenged elude His sight.

A-wretch, what plea then shall I name,
What advocate make bold to claim,
When scarce the just escape the fiame?
O King majestic, roved in fear,
Who freely sav'st Thy people dear,
Bring me, Thou Fount of pity, clear.

For me, good Jesu, think, I pray,
Thou once didst tread Thy bitter way:
O let me not be lost that ay!
To gain me, Thou didst sink outworn
To ransom me. the Cross hast borne
Such travail lost ne'er may I mourn!

Just Judge, Who wilt for vengeance rise,
O grant me pardon's precious prize,
Before the Day of Great Assize.
I groan as if this hour arraigned
My scarlet cheek with guilt is stained:
Thy suitor, Lord, be not disdained!

Thou freed'st a sinner from her fear
Thou lentest to a thief Thine ear;
To me. too, gavest hope to cheer.
My prayers are worthless, but do Thou
In grace and mercy ne'er allow
That I to deathless fire should bow.

Grant me among the sheep to stand
Disjoin me from the goats' dark band,
And set me down at Thy right hand.
What time the cursed, dumb with shame
Are sentenced to the piercing flame,
Then with the blest O call my name!

In lowly trustfulness I pray
'Fore Thee a broken heart I lay:
O be at death my Guard and Stay!
That hour is rife with bitter tears,
Wherein mankind, amid their fears,
Shall rise again from ashy biers.

When judgment on his sin is pressed,
God spare the sinner, sore distressed
To all, good Jesu, grant Thy rest.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Zion, at thy shining gates
verses:
Zion, at thy shining gates,
Lo! the King of Glory waits
Haste thy Monarch's pomp to greet.
Strew thy palms before His feet!

Christ, for Thee their triple light,
Faith, and Hope, and Love unite;
This the beacon we display.
To proclaim Thine Advent Day.

Give us grace Thy yoke to wear
Give us strength Thy Cross to bear;
Make us Thine in deed and word,
Thine in heart and life, O Lord.

Kill in us the carnal root,
That the Spirit may bear fruit
Plant in us Thy lowly mind
Keep us faithful, loving, kind.

So, when Thou shalt come again.
Judge of angels and of men
We, with all Thy saints, shall sing
Hallelujahs to our King.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: BEHOLD! the Baptist's warning sounds
verses:
BEHOLD! the Baptist's warning sounds
Thrill through the Jordan's winding
bounds As grass that fades, our mortal rac
As rings his herald voice on high.
Let listless slumber quickly fly!
The heaven, the ocean, and the earth,
Their great Creator's coming birth
See rising on their longing sight,
And greet it with supreme delight

Thou, Jesu, Thou our safety art,
The strength and balm of every heart:

Lies pining for Thy absent Face
if Stretch forth Thy Hand the sick to

Lift up the fall'n; Thy face reveal
Its own fair beauty now, once more,
Let bloom upon this earthly floor.

To Him, Who comes the world to free,
To Son, and Fatuer, honour be
Thee, gracious Spirit, we adore,
From age to age, for evermore.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The Lord will come! the earth shall quake
verses:
The Lord will come! the earth shall quake,
The hills their fixed seat forsake
And, withering, from the vault of night
The stars withdraw their feeble light.

The Lord will come! but not the same
As once in lowly form He came,
A silent Lamb to slaughter Jed,
The bruised, the suffering, and the dead.

The Lord will come! a dreadful Form,
With wreath of fiame, and robe of storm,
On cherub wings, and wings of wind,
Anointed Judge of human kind!

Can this be He, Who wont to stray
A pilgrim on the world's highway
By power oppressed, and mocked by pride?
Oh God! is this the Crucified

Go, tyrants! to the rocks complain!
Go, seek the mountains cleft in vain!
But 'aith, victorious o'er the tomb,
Shall sing for joy: 'The Lord is come!”
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord, give us of that fervent love
verses:
Lord, give us of that fervent love,
That warm effusion from above,
Which filled Thy servant's breast,
When hearing Thou must quit his view,
He mourned that he no pathway knew,
To trace Thee to Thy Rest.

When Thou wert nailed, and pierced, and dead,
Upon the curséd tree that spread
Its arms to paling light,
Still loving Thee, he sadly wept
Those bleeding scars the steel had left,
Deep graven on his sight.

Then, sorely haunted by the view,
When sound the tidings, glad and true,
That Thou art raised again:
Save I can see and feel,” he cries,
''Those wounds, fast printed on mine eyes,
The tidings sound in vain.”

Thou callest him, as mute he stands,
To feel and see Thy Side, Thine Hands:
“My Lord! my God!” breaks out:
'Thee, Thomas, sight to Faith doth draw;
More blest are they who never saw,
Yet never knew a doubt.”

Good Lord, Who didst desery the spot,
Where he was marred by carnal blot,
Though loving to the last;
O grant, by Faith we may be stayed,
His soft rebuke our saving aid,
t On Truth our anchor cast.

Har! the herald angels sing
Glory to the new-born King!
Peace on earth, and mercy mild,
God and sinners reconciled
Joyful, all ye nations, rise,
Join the triumph in the skies!
Universal nature say,
Curis the Lord is born to-day.

Curzist, by highest Heaven adored
Cuzist, the everlasting Lord;
Late in time behold Him come,
Offspring of a Virgin's womb!
Veiled in flesh the Godhead see!
Hail, th' incarnate Deity
Pleased as Man with men t'appear,

Light and life to all He brings,
Ris'n with healing in His wings.
Mild He lays His Glory by,
Born that man no more may die,
Born to raise the sons of earth,
Born to give them second birth.

Come, Drsrre of Nations, come,
Fix in us Thy humble home!
Rise, the Woman's conquering Seed,
Bruise in us the Serpent's head!
Now display Thy saving Power,
Ruined nature now restore;
Now in mystic union join
Thine to ours, and ours to Thine!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Mescy triumphs, Cagist is born
verses:
Mescy triumphs, Cagist is born
Seraphs hail this happy morn!
Eeho loud their solemn cry:
“Glory be to God on high!"

Praise to God, and peace on earth
Such the tidings of His birth:
Him we worship, Him we bless,
Prince of Peace and Righteousness.

Promised Branch of Jesse's stem,
Cuaist is born in Bethlehem!
'We have pardon, we have peace;
Darkness, guilt, and terror cease.

Light and mercy cheer the tomb!
Hallelujah! Crist is come!
Let all earth's redeemed cry:
I “Glory be to God on high!"

Son of May, He murmured not,
Bore with us, and shared our lot;
Sow of God, we know Him well,
By each sign the prophets tell.

His the love to feel our woe;
His the might to quell our foe:
Unto Hin, in earth and heaven,
Be all praise and honour given!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: AxGEts from the realms of glory
verses:
AxGEts from the realms of glory,
Wing your flight o'er all the earth!
Ye, who sang Creation's story,
Now proclaim Messiah's birth:
Come and worship,
Worship Carist, the new-born King!

Shepherds, in the field abiding,
Watching oer your flocks by night,
God with man is now residing,
Yonder shines the infant-light:
Come and worship,
Worship Cuzist, the new-born King!

Sages, leave your contemplations,
Brighter visions beam afar;
Scek the great Desire of nations,
Ye have seen His natal star:
Come and worship,
Worship Christ, the new-born King!

Saints, before the altar bending,
Watching long in hope and fear,
Suddenly the Lord, descending,
In His Temple shall appear;
Come and worship,
Worship Christ, the new-born King!

Sinners, wrung with true repentance,
Doomed for guilt to endless pains,
Justice now revokes the sentence,
Mercy calls you: break your chains
Come and worship,
Worship Christ, the new-born King!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Bricut and joyfal is the morn
verses:
Bricut and joyfal is the morn,
For to us a Child is born;
From the highest realms of Heaven,
Unto us a Son is given.

On His shoulder He shall bear
Power and Majesty, and wear
On His vesture, and His thigh,
Names most awful, names most high.

Come and worship at His feet,
Yield to Cagist the homage meet:
From His manger to His throne,
Homage due to God alone.

Glory be to God on high!
Earth, uplift the joyful cry!
Praise Him, all ye heavenly host,
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Waite shepherds watched their flocks by night
verses:
Waite shepherds watched their flocks by night,
All seated on the ground,
The angel of the Lord came down,
And glory shone around.
'Fear not,” said he; (for mighty dread
Had seized their troubled mind
Glad tidings of great
To you and all mankii in y

“To you, in David's town, this day
Is born of David's line,
The Saviovk, Who is Curtst the Lord;
And this shall be the sign:
'The heavenly Babe you there shall find
To human view displaye
All meanly wrapt in swaddling bands,
And in a manger laid.”

Thus spake the Seraph; and forthwith
ppeared a shining throng
Of angels, praising God, and thus
Addressed their joyful song:
“All gio be to God on high,
And te the earth be peace;
Good will henceforth from Heaven to men
Begin, and never cease!”
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Hare! What mean those holy voices
verses:
Hare! What mean those holy voices,
Sweetly warbling in the skies?
Sure th' angelic host rejoices;
Loudest hallelujabs rise.

Listen to the wondrous story,
Which they chant in hymns 27f joy:
F Glory in the highest, glory;
Glory be to God most high.

Peace on earth, good will from heaven,
Reaching far as man is found;
Souls redeemed and sins forgiven,
Loud our golden harps shall sound

Christ is born, the great Anointed!
Heaven and earth His glory sing!
Glad receive Whom God appointed
For your Prophet, Priest, and King.

Hasten, mortals, to adore Him;
Learn His Name, and taste His joy
Till in heaven you sing before Him,
Glory be to God most High.

Let us learn the wondrous story
Of our great REDEEMER's birth;
Spread the brightness of His glory
Till it cover al] the earth.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Come! Thou long-expected Jesus
verses:
Come! Thou long-expected Jesus!
Born to set Thy people free!
From our cares and sins release us;
Let us find our rest in Thee.

Israel's strength and consolation!
Hope of all the earth Thou art!
Blest desire of every nation!
Joy of every longing heart!

Born, Thy people to deliver!
Born a Child, and yet a King!
Born, to reign in us for ever!
Now Thy gracious Kingdom bring.

By Thine Own Eternal Spirit,
Rule in all our hearts alone;
By Thine all-sufficient merit,
Raise us to Thy glorious Throne!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Jesu, life of ruined man
verses:
O Jesu, life of ruined man,
With God the Father One,
His equal ere the world began,
Now born His only Son:

Tho Peace, the only Hope art Thou
Of sinners sore distrest
Hear every earnest prayer and vow,
From every burdened breast.

In mortal form, for mortals' sake,
Thou didst Thyself enshrine:
O grant that we, too, may partake
Thy Nature, pure, divine.
Thus raised to such an honoured state, ff O Jesu, Virgin-born, with Thee
O guard us, Lord most high!
Lest we, beneath temptation's weight,
Relapse to sin, and die,

This grace we crave, on this high day,
Which speaks Thy glorious birth,
When Thou, true Sun, didst shed Thy ray,
To light the gloomy earth.

The land, the sky, the mighty sea,
In rivalry shall raise
To Him, Whose love hath giv'n us Thee,
Glad songs of holy praise;

And we, for whom Thou hast been born,
Of endless life the Spring,
Will magnify this bless¢d Morn,
And hymns of triumph sing.

The Father we adore
To God the Spirit, Sacred Three,
Be glory evermore!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Chief of Martyrs! thou, whose name
verses:
Chief of Martyrs! thou, whose name
Doth a mystic Crown proclaim,
Not of flowers that see decay,
Weave we this thy Crown to-day.

Red the stones thy blood engrains,
Shining fairer for the stains
Studded round thy saintly head,
Stars could ne'er such lustre shed.

Where the wounds thy forehead gash;
Darts of light divinely fiash
Bursting from thy brow, each ray
Doth an angel-face betray.

First of victims, thou with life
Carist dost honour in the strife
First Confessor, whose last breath
Flies to own Him God in death.

First to tread the crimson sea,
O'er the pathway marked for thee!
Thou the foremost to the view!
Lo! the Martyr-host pursue!

Virgin-born, to Thee we raise,
With the Father, ceaseless praise
God the Spirit we adore,
Age on age, for evermore.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: THY dear disciple on the sea
verses:
THY dear disciple on the sea,
A son of labour rude and sore,
Leaves ship and sire, O Lord, for

This, toil and love in sweet embrace,
He lives to cheer Thy weary breast,
A meet companion in Thy race:
Thy bosom, pillow of his rest.

Though there he lay in wistful love,
He courts no ianguor, dull and

But soars an eagle, sinks a dove;
All fervid, soft, sublime and meek.

That tender heart, that ardent mind,
Such honour reaped as none have

Thy dying lips to him consigned
Thy Bless¢d Mother for his own.

Full long the toil of life his lot:
Peace! let him tarry till [come!"
'Come, Lord! Draw near this lonely spot,
And take Thy waiting martyr home.”

Thus calm, may we abide the hour,
Thy Face revealing from above;
Still zealous, though with waning power
While strength declines, still firm in
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Aut hail! ye martyr-blooms so bright
verses:
Aut hail! ye martyr-blooms so bright,
Which, opening to the rising light,
The sword mowed down with cruel
blade, The Christ, is rescued for His throne.
As rosebuds 'neath the tempest laid.
The first for Curis to shed your blood,
A tender flock, its crimson flood
Ye artless by the altar stray;
With palm and chaplet blithely play.

The fell assassin, sword in hand,
In fury slays the infant band;
Each frame, so lately born to light,
Is ransacked for the quickening sprite.

What gain in guilt of such a dve?
What booted Herod crime so high?
*Mid deaths so many, One alone,

Amid the purple rills that run
From hearts of babes, the Virgin's

Alone unharmed, defies the blow,
That sinks bereavéd mothers low.

Then, Virgin-born, to Thee we raise,
With Thee, O Faruer, endless praise
Thee, Hoxy Spirit, we adore,
From age to age, for evermore.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Blest day, on which the Saviour shed
verses:
Blest day, on which the Saviour shed
High sanctity, as first He bled!
Blest day, whereon He first began
The task to ransom fallen man!

Scarce born to light, behold! His blood
The Babe outpours. a tender flood
The foretaste of a deadly strife
The opening of a loving life.

Earth now His home, with fervid will
His Fatser's mandates to fulfil,
He quick forestalls His day decreed,
And learus, a Victim, how to bleed.

Before that wound, which it had made,
The cancelled law is seen to fade;
A purer law begins to reign,
The love, which deathless shall remain.

Thou, Curisr, within our hearts, this day
What is not Thine cut clean away;
O write Thy Name, that law of Thine,
Within our bosoms' inmost shrine.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Let tyrants take their haughty names
verses:
Let tyrants take their haughty names,
From nations forced to bleed
A nobler title Christ assumes
From those that He hath freed.

None other name than this is giv'n
For mortals to adore;
A Name throngh which the dead revive,
And live for evermore.

The purchase, made at such a cost,
When all His blood was spilt,
Are we again, in mad affront,
To cancel by our guilt?

Thou, Who dost love to be invoked
Blest Saviour of us all!
In Thy great Name we make our boast
O hear us when we call!

Great Jesu, from the Virgin born,
We glory give to Thee;
The Father and the Spiait praise,
Till ages cease to be.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The num'rous train of ills disclose
verses:
The num'rous train of ills disclose,
Which this frail state attend.

My life Thou know'st is but a span,
A cypher sums my years;
And every man, in best estate,
But vanity appears.

Why then should I on worthless toy
With anxious care attend?
On Thee alone my steadfast hope,
Shall ever, Lord, depend.

Lest my frail flesh too weak to bear
The heavy load should prove.

Lord, hear my cry, accept my tears,
And listen to my prayer;
Who sojourn like a stranger here,
As all my fathers were

O spare me yet a little time;
My wasted strength restore
Before I vanish qnite from hence,
And shall be scen no more.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Father, let me dedicate
verses:
Father, let me dedicate
All this year to Thee,
In whatever worldly state
Thou wilt have me be.
Not from sorrow, pain, or care,
Freedom dare I claim
This alone shall be my prayer:

Can a child presume to choose
Where or how to live?
Can a Father's love refuse
All the best to give?
More Thou givest every day
Than the best can claim;
Nor witholdest ought that may
t “Glorify Thy Name!”

my If in mercy Thou wilt spare
Joys that yet are mine;
If on life, serene and fair,
Brighter rays may shine;
Let my heart, while glad it sings,
Thee in all proclaim
And, whate'er the future brings,
I “ Glorify Thy Name!"

If Thou callest to the Cross,
And its shadow come,
Turning all my gain to loss,
Shrouding heart and home,
Let me think how Thy dear Son
To His glory came,
And, in deepest woe, pray on,
t “Glorify Thy Name!”
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: For Thy mercy and Thy grace
verses:
For Thy mercy and Thy grace,
Faithful throngh another year,
Hear our song of thankfulness,
FaTHrr, and REDEEMER, hear!

In our weakness and distress,
Rock of Strengtb, be Thou our Stay!
In the pathless wilderness
Be our true and living way!

Who of us death's awful road
In the coming year shall tread?
With Thy rod and staff, O God,
Comfort Tnou his dying bed.

Keep us faithfal, keep us pure.
eep us evermore Thine Own!
Help, O help us to endure!
Fit us for the promised crown}

So within Thy palace gate
We shall praise. on golden striugs,
Thee, the only Potentate,
Lord of lords, and Krixe of kings!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Harp, awake! tell out the story
verses:
Harp, awake! tell out the story
Of our love, and joy, and praise
Lute, awake! awake our glory!
Join a thankful song to raise!
Join we, brethren faithful-hearted,
Lift the solemn voice again
O'er another year departed
Of our threescore years and ten.

ny Gracious Saviour, Thou hast lengthened,
And hast blest our mortal span,
And in our weak hearts hast strengthened
What Thy grace alone began!
Still, when danger shall betide us,
Be Thy warning whisper heard;
Keep us at Thy feet, and guide us
By Thy Spirit, and Thy Word!

Let Thy favour and Thy blessing
Crown the year we now begin;
Let us all, Thy strength possessing,
Grow in grace, and vanquish sin!
Storms are round us, hearts are quailing,
Signs in heaven, and earth and sea;
But when heaven and earth are failing,
Saviour! we will trust in Thee.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Or noble cities thou art Queen
verses:
Or noble cities thou art Queen;
Thou, Bethlehem, alone hast seen
Salvation's Captain, from the sky,
Incarnate in a cradle lie.

The star, before whose lustre bright,
The sun, out-matched, now dims his light,
Proclaims that God has come to earth,
A fieshly Form of human birth.

Him soon as e'er the Magi saw,
Their Eastern off rings forth they draw,
And, prostrate, with their prayers unfold
Myrrh, fi

The treasure, and the scented smell
Of Saba's incense, loudly tell
His Kingship, Godbead; while the myrrh
Speaks sadly of His sepulchre.

All glory be to Jesu's Name,
A bright Epiphany Who came
To FarueRr, Spreit, high we raise,
From age to age, unceasing praise.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: As with gladness men of old
verses:
As with gladness men of old
Did the guiding star behold;
As with joy they hailed its light,
Leading onward, beaming bright
So, most gracious God, may we
Evermore be led by Thee.

As with joyful steps they sped
To that lowly manger-bed,
There to bend the Knee before
Him, Whom heaven and earth adore;
So may we, with willing feet,
Ever seek Thy mercy-seat.

As they offered gifts most rare
At that manger, rude and bare;
So may we, with holy joy,
Pure and free from sin's alloy,
All our costliest treasures bring,
Christ, to Thee, our heavenly King.

Holy Jesus! every day
eep us in the narrow way
And, when earthly things are past,
Bring our ransomed souls at last
Where they need no star to guide,
Where no clouds Thy glory hide.

In the heavenly country bright,
Need they no created light
Thou its Life, its Joy, its Crown,
Thou its Sun, which goes not down;
There for ever may we sing
Alleluias to our King!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Waar star is this that beams so bright
verses:
Waar star is this that beams so bright,
The sun eclipsing in his might?
It doth the new-born Krxe display
To find His cradle points the way.

On ancient prophets Faith depends;
See! Jacob's Star on high ascends!
Arrested at the heavenly blaze,
Starts forth the East in deep amaze.

Without, the Star informs their sight,
Within, there shines a brighter light,
Which leads them, by its gentle force,
To trace the marvel to its source.

Love never knows of dull delays
Toil, dangers, nought, alarm can raise;
Their home, their kip, their native land,
They promptly quit at God's command.

While beams the Star of Mercy pure,
And Thou our hearts dost still allure,
Grant, Lord, in sloth they re'er may pine,
Nor quench the light that burns divine.

To Thee, O FarHeEr, Radiance bright,
To Thee, O Son. the nations' Light,
Be praise eternal, and to Thee,
O Sprit, equal glory be.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: God of mercy, God of grace
verses:
God of mercy, God of grace,
Shew the brightness of Thy face
Shine upon us, Saviour, shine
Fill Thy Church with light divine
And Thy saving health extend
Unto earth's remotest end,

Let the people praise Thee, Lord!
Be by all that live adored!
Let the nations shout and sing
Glory to their Saviour Krxe!
At Thy feet their tribute pay,
And Thy holy will obey!

Soxs of men, behold from far!
Hail the long-expected star!
Jacob's star, that gilds the night,
Guides bewildered Nature right.

Fear not hence that ill should fiow,
Wars or pestilence below
Wars it bids and tumults cease,
Ush'ring in the Prince of Peace.

Mild He shines on all beneath,
Piercing through the shades of death;
Scatt'ring error's wide-spread night,
Kindling darkness into hgbt.

Nations all, far off and near,
Haste to see your God appear!
Haste! for Him your hearts prepare;
Meet Him manifested there!

Here behold the Day-spring rise,
Pouring eyesight on your eyes!
God in His Own light survey,
Shining to the perfect day!

Sing, ye morning stars again,
God descends on earth to reign;
Deigns for man His life t'employ:
Shout, ye sons of God, for joy
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The race, that long in darkness pined
verses:
The race, that long in darkness pined,
Have seen a glorious light;
The people dwell in day, who dwelt
In death's surrounding night,

To hail Thy rise, Thou better San,
The gath'ring nations come,
With joy, as when the reapers bear
The harvest-treasures home.

my For Thou our burden hast removed,
And quelled th' oppressor's sway,
As quick as slaughtered squadrons fell
In Midian's evil day.

JS To us a Child cf hope is born,
To us a Son is given:
The tribes of earth shall Him obey,
Him all the hosts of heaven.

His Name shall be the Prince of Peace,
For evermore adored,
The Wonderful, the Counsellar,
The great and mighty Lord!

His power increasing still shall spread,
His reign no end shall know:
His throne shall justice guard above,
And peace abound below.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: AuLetvra! song of sweetness
verses:
Sf Alleluia! Satem, Mother,
Glad thou dost the chorus sing,
Alleluia! 'tis the homage,
Which thy sons in triumph bring!
Babylon, from us, sad exiles,
By her waters, tears doth wring.

Alleluia we, unworthy,
May not always lift on high;
Alleluia, our transgressions
Check the utt'rance, as we cry:
Comes the hour for deeply mourning
Sins, that heavy on us lie.

Thee, in this our adoration,
Blesséd Trinity. we pray:
Grant us in the blissful mansions
Visions of Thine Easter-day
There to sing to Thee with rapture
Alleluia's sweetest lay.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Sones of praise the angels sang
verses:
Sones of praise the angels sang,
Heaven with hallelujahs rang,
When JEHOVAR's work begun,
When He spake, and it was done.

Songs of praise awoke the morn,
When the Prixce of Pkace was born;
Songs of praise arose, when He
Captive led captivity.

Heaven and earth must pass away:
Songs of praise shall crown that day;
God will make new heavens and earth:
Songs of praise shall hail their birth.

And can man alone be dumb,
Till that glorious kingdom come
No; the Church delights to raise
Psalms and hymns, and songs of praise.

Saints below, with heart and voice,
Still in songs of praise rejoice;
Learning here, by faith and love,
Songs of praise to sing above.

Borne upon their latest breath,
Songs of praise shall conquer death;
en, amidst eternal joy,
Songs of praise their powers employ.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The Lord, He gave the Word
verses:
The Lord, He gave the Word!
The Void quick heard the sound,
And Matter straight from nothing rose,
Fast riveted in dead repose,
Till rings a voice around:
Light beams afar!
Sun, moon, and star!
Lo! in the rear
See Man appear,
Thrice noble form! God's image dear!

The Lord, He gave the Word!
The sound is heard within:
Soft steals the Saviour to the heart,
To calm and cure the bleeding smart,
And blot away its sin:
Then rend the skies
With pealing cries!
High songs of praise
Triumphant raise!
The Lord extol to endless days!

The Lord, He gave the Word!
Loud rose the preachers' cry!
The heathen tremble at the tone,
And Satan shudders on his throne
The powers of darkness fly!
t Each idol stoops
All evil droops
No foes remain;
The Lord doth reign;
The world is His from mount to plain.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Goop Lord, Who hast the weighty woes
verses:
Goop Lord, Who hast the weighty woes
Of galling trial borne,
Regard Thy servants' bitter throes,
While wrestling with their cruel foes,
Dejected, wasted, worn.

Remember that once happy spot,
Within whose tainted pale
The serpent, jealous at their lot,
Contrived to fix a lasting blot
On man and woman frail.

Thus lost, O woman's Holy Seed,
When comes the Tempter nigh,
Confound his counsel, thwart his deed,
Lest we, his fallen victims, bleed,
And 'neath his rancour die.

Vouchsafe us patience, loving Lord,
To ease this mortal strife;
Oh! utter forth Thy sovereign word,
That Cherubim may sheathe the sword,
Which guards the Tree of Life.

Grant us to eat its golden fruits,
And drink the living stream,
That washes by its holy roots,
As high it lifts its healing shoots,
To greet the heavenly beam.

May we, our race of trial run,
Safe landed on the shore,
Thy glorious triumph now begun,
An Eden lost, an Eden won,
Find rest for evermore!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lo! steals apace the welcome tide
verses:
Lo! steals apace the welcome tide,
Sweet safety's dawning hour,
When Mercy's gate will open wide
To catch the mourner's shower.

Then use with ever softened zest
Thy words, thy food, thy sleep
Check mirth, and with a keener breast
Thy daily vigil keep.

Let grief, unbosomed from the heart,
On tears, that gushing fall,
Feed sadly; yet, despite the smart,
Approach the Judge of al

With zeal pursue the path that leads
To dwellings cold and rude,
Where droop the poor, where sorrow bleeds,
And Christ is faint for food

Here, stretching forth a lavish hand.
Let love her wealth outpour
Consign it to a heavenly land.
Lest death should seize the store.

Lord, consecrate us all to Thee,
With newly kindled love,
That purer thoughts, where'er we be,
May flame to heav'n above.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Tux solemn time of holy fast
verses:
Tux solemn time of holy fast
To mourning sadly calls;
Lo! weeps the priest! and tearful cries
Ring round the temple walls.

In vain ascend the toues of grief,
Heav'n's angered ear to seek,
Unless the utt'rance of the soul
An inward sorrow speak.

In vain the sprinkled ashes fall,
The robe is rent in vain,
Unless the heavy-laden heart
Is torn with living pain.

Then let us kneel, in truest woe,
To stay the wrath of God,
Who, knowing all our sore misdeeds,
Suspends His threat'ning rod.

To punishment be slow
Grant penitential hours and hearts
Avert the menaced blow.

Blest Tarstrr! Great Trrzx in One!
O grant Thy suff'ring race,
To reap from these, our lowly fasts,
The blooming fruits of grace.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: My God, my God, my Light, my Love
verses:
My God, my God, my Light, my Love,
Mine all in all to me,
Wilt Thou a gracious Father prove
To souls that hang on Thee?

My God, my God, my Light, my Love,
For Thee I thirst alone;
The sweetest waters on the earth
My soul accounts as none.

My God, my God, my Light, my Love,
Mine only, only Friend,
I seek, I long, I look for Thee:
Why wilt Thou not attend?

My God, my God, my Light, my Love,
Oh! whither art Thou gone?
Either be near unto me here,
Or lift me to Thy Throne.

My God, my God, my Light, my Love,
Canst Thou that soul forsake,
That follows Thee with restless cries,
And longs to overtake.

My God, my God, my Light, my Love,
Hear Thou my mournful cry:
The God of Love hears from above;
He will not see me die.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Come, let us to the Lord our God
verses:
Come, let us to the Lord our God
With contrite hearts return
Our God is gracious, nor will leave
The desolate to mourn.

His voice commands the tempest forth,
And stills the stormy wave;
And though His arm be strong to smite,
*Tis also strong to save.

The night of sorrow long hath reigned
The dawn shall bring us light;
For God appears, and we shall rise
With gladness in His sight.

Our hearts, if God we seek to know,
Shall know Him and rejoice;
His coming like the morn shall be,
Like morning songs His voice.

As dew upon the tender herb,
Diffusing fragrance round;
As show'rs that usher in the spring,
And cheer the thirsty ground:

So shall His presence bless our souls,
And shed a joyfal light;
That hallowed morn shall chase away
The sorrows of the night.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Iy the hour of trial
verses:
Iy the hour of trial,
Jzsus, pray for me:
Lest by base denial
I depart from Thee
When Thou seest me waver,
With a look recall,
Nor for fear or favor
Suffer me to fall.

With forbidden pleasures
Would this vain world charm
Or its sordid treasures
Spread to work me harm;
Bring to my remembrance
Bad Gethsemane,
Or, in darker semblance,
é ross-crowned Calvary.

When my last hour cometh,
Fraught with strife and pain;
When my dust returneth
To the dust again;
cres, On Thy truth relying,
Through that mortal strife,
JxEsws, take me dying
To eternal life.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: From lowest depths of woe
verses:
From lowest depths of woe
To God I sent my cry:
Lord, hear my supplicating voice,
And graciously reply.
Should'st Thou severely judge,
Who can the trial bear?
But Thou forgiv'st, lest we despond, The plenteoussource and spring, from whence
And quite renounce Thy fear.

My soul with patience waits
For Thee, the living Lord
My hopes are on Thy promise built,
And never-failing word.

My longing eyes look out
For Thy enliv'ning ray,
More duly than the morning watch
To spy the dawning day.
JS Let Israel trust in God,
No bounds His mercy knows:

Whose friendly streams to us
Supplies in want convey:
A healing spring, a spring to cleanse,
And wash our guilt away.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: WHEN our heads are bowed with woe
verses:
WHEN our heads are bowed with woe,
'When our bitter tears o'erflow,
When we mourn the lost, the dear,
Gracious Son of Mary, hear!

When the sullen death-bell tolls
For our own departed souls!
When our final doom is near.
Gracious Soy of Mary, hear!

Thou hast bowed the dying head;
Thou the blood of life hast shed
Thou hast filled a mortal bier!
Gracious Son of Mary, hear!

When the heart is sad within,
With the thought of all its sin;
When the spirit shrinks with fear,
Gracious Son of Mary, hear!

Thou the shame, the grief hast known,
Though the sins were not Thine Own:
Thou hast deigned their load to bear:
Gracious Son of Mary, hear!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Lord, turn not Thy face from me
verses:
O Lord, turn not Thy face from me,
Who lie in woeful state,
Lamenting all my sinful life
Before Thy mercy-gate
A gate which opens wide to those
That do lament their sin;
Shut not that gate against me, Lord,
But let me enter in,

And call me not to strict account,
How I have sojourned here;
For then my guilty conscience knows
How vile I shall appear.
So come I to Thy mer -gate
Where mercy doth abound,
Imploring pardon for my sin,
To heal my deadly wound.

Good Lord, I mercy, mercy ask,
This is the total sum;
For mercy, Lord, is all my suit:
Lord, let Thy mercy come!
To Faruer, Son, and Hoty Ghost,
The God, Whom we adore,
Be glory, as it was, is now,
And shall be evermore.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Ovwitr Thou pardon, Lord
verses:
Ovwitr Thou pardon, Lord,
A sinner such as I,
Although Thy book his crimes record
Of such a crimson dye?

So deep are they engraved!
So terrible their fear!
The righteous ecarcely shall be saved,
And where shall I appear?

know not how to praise
Thy mercy and Thy love.
But deign Thy servant to upraise,
And I shall learn above.

My soul, make all things known
To Him, Who all things sees:
That so the Lamp may yet atone
For thine iniquities.

O Thou Physician blest,
Make clean my guilty soul,
And me, by many a sin oppressed,
Restore, and keep me whole.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: P Have mercy, Lord, on me
verses:
P Have mercy, Lord, on me,
As Thou wert ever kind
Let me, oppressed with loads of guilt,
Thy wonted mercy find.

mye Wash off my foul offence,
And cleanse me from my sin
For I confess my crime, and see

By God most highly prized
By Him a broken, contrite heart
Shall never be despised.

Withdraw not Thou Thy help,

Its everlasting flight.

The joy Thy favour gives
Let me again obtain;
And Thy free Spreir's firm support
My fainting soul sustain.

To God, the Fatuer, Son,
And Spirit, glory be;
As was, and is, and shall be so,
To all eternity.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord, when we bend before Thy throne
verses:
Lord, when we bend before Thy throne,
And our confessions pour,
Teach us to feel the sins we own,
And hate what we deplore.

Our broken spirits, pitying, see,
And penitence impart;
Then let a kindling glance from Thee
Beam hope upon the heart.

When onr responsive tongues essay
Their grateful hymns to raise,
Grant that our souls may join the lay,
And mount to Thee in praise.

When we disclose our wants in prayer,
May we our wills resign;
Ani not a thought our bosom share,
Which is not wholly Thine.

Let faith each meek petition fill,
And waft it to the skies;
And teach our hearts 'tis goodness still,
That grants it or denies.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: THERE is a Fountain, filled with Llood
verses:
THERE is a Fountain, filled with Llood,
Drawn from Emmanuel's Veins;
And sinners, plunged beneath that flood,
Lose all their guilty stains,

The dying thief rejoiced to see
That Fountain in his day
And there may I, as well as he,
Wash all my sins away.

Then in a nobler, sweeter song,
I'll sing Thy power to save,
When this poor, lispinz, stammering tongue
P Lies silent in the grave.

O Lame of God! Thy precious Blood
Shall never lose its power,
Till all the ransomed Church of God
Be saved, to sin no more.

E'er since, by faith, I saw the stream
Thy flowing wounds supply,
Redeeming love has been my theme,
And shall be till I die.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: JESUS, cast a look on me
verses:
All that feeds my busy pride,
Cast it evermore aside
Bid my will to Thine snbmit;
Lay me humbly at Thy feet.

Make me like a little child,
Of my strength and wisdom spoiled,
Seeing only in Thy light,
Walking only in Thy might;

Leaning on Thy loving breast,
Where a weary soul may rest;
Feeling well the peace of God,
Flowing from Thy precious blood.

In this posture let me live,
And hosannas daily give:
In this temper let me die,
And hosannas ever cry!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: WHEN rising from the bed of death
verses:
WHEN rising from the bed of death,
O'erwhelmed with guilt and fear,
I see my Maker face to face,
O how shall I appear!

If yet, while pardon may be found,
And mercy may be sought,
My heart with inward horror shrinks,
And trembles at the thought.

When Thou, O Lord, shalt stand disclosed
In majesty severe,
And sit in judgment on my soul,
O how shall I appear!

But Thou hast told the troubled sonl,
Who does her sins lament,
The timely tribute of her tears
Shall endless woe prevent.

Then see the sorrows of my heart,
Ere yet it be too late,
And add my Saviour's dying groans,
To give those sorrows weight.

For never shall my soul despair
Her pardon to procure,
Who knows Thy only Son has died
To make that pardon sure.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: God, my Father, hear me pray
verses:
God, my Father, hear me pray,
Wa-h my crimson guilt away;
Wretched, helpless, lost, undone,
Hear me for Thy blesséd Sox.
Lord, unnumbered sins are mine,
cres, But eternal love is Thine.

God my Comforter, my Light,
Strengthen me with holy might,
Make Thy dwelling in my heart;
Faith, a: d joy, and hope impart.
Lord, unnumbered sins are mine,
But eternal love is Thine.

S Blesséd, glorious Trinity!
Holy, everla-ti g THREE!
Hear, O hear my earn-st prayer,
And my soul for heaven prepare.
Lord, unnumbered sins are mine,
But eternal love is Thine.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: SAviour, when in dust to Thee
verses:
SAviour, when in dust to Thee
Low we bend th' adoring knee;
When repentant to the skies
Scarce we lift our weeping eyes
peres. Oh! by all Thy pains and woe,
Suffered once for man below,
Bending from Thy Throne on high,
bp Hear our solemn Litany!

By Thy deep expiring groan;
By the sad sepulchral stone
By the vault, whose dark abode
Held in vain the rising God;
crs. Ob! from earth to heaven restored,
Mighty re-ascended Lord,
Listen, listen to the ery
Of our solemn Litany!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The kingly banners onward stream
verses:
The kingly banners onward stream,
And shines the Cross with mystic beam,
Where man's Creator, flesh to free, é r
In flesh lies hanging on the Tree.

Lo! wounded doth He there appear,
Deep stricken by the pointed spear,
'To wash the sinner in the flood,
Outpouring water, mixed with blood.

The Tree, how beautcous and how bright!
With royal purple richly dight!
Culled from a stock of noble race,
Those limbs so sacred to embrace.

Blest Tree! the balanee where there hung
The costly price, from justice wrung,
The ransom for a world to pay,
Aud tear from Hell its rifled prey.

O Blessed Lord, our only stay
In this Thy Passion's rueful day,
In holy hearts Thy grace implant,
And pardon to the sinner grant.

O Trinity, Great God most High,
Let every breath Thy praises cry
And whom the mystic Cross doth free,
Rule Thou to all eternity!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Frow the deeps of grief and fear
verses:
Frow the deeps of grief and fear,
Lord, to Thee my seul repairs:
From Thy heav'n bow down Thine ear;
Let Thy mercy meet my prayers.
Oh! if Thou mara'st what's done amiss,

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Wake, O my soul! awake and raise
verses:
Wake, O my soul! awake and raise
Thine every part to sing His praise.
Who from His sphere of glory fell,
To raise thee up from death and hell
See how His soul, vext for thy sin,
Weeps blood without, feels hell within!

Wake, O mine eyes! awake, and view
These two twin lights, whence heavens drew
Their glorious beams, whose gracious sight
Fills you with joy, with life, and light
See how, with clouds of sorrow drowned,
They wash with tears thy sinful wound!

Wake, O mine ear! awake, and hear
That pow'rful voice, which stills thy fear,
And brings from heaven those joyful news,
Which heaven commands, which hell subdues;
Hark! how His ears, heav''n's mercy-seat,
Foul slanders with reproaches beat!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: RrvE on! ride on in majesty
verses:
RrvE on! ride on in majesty!
Hark! all the tribes Hosanna cry!
Thine humble beast pursues his road,
With palms and scattered garments strowed.

Ride on! ride on in majesty!
In lowly pomp ride on to die!
O Christ, Thy triumphs now begin
F O'er captive death and cunquered sin.

Ride on! ride on in majesty!
The wing?d squadrons of the sky
Look down with sad an: wondering eyes,
To see th' approaching Sacrifice.

Ride on! ride on in majesty!
Thy last and fiercest strife is nigh,
The FATHER, on His sapphire throne,
Expects His Own anointed Soy.

Ride on! ride on in majesty!
In lowly pomp ride on to die!
Bow Thy meek Head to mortal pain:
i Then take, O God, Thy power and reign!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Rock of Ages, cleft for me
verses:
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let ine hide myself in Thee;
Let the water and the blood
From Thy riven side which flowed
Be of sin the double cure,
Cleanse me from its guilt and power

While I draw this fleeting breath,
When my eyestrings break in death.
When I soar through tracts unknown,
See Thee on Thy judgment-throne;
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Wxo comes from Edom, with His robes
verses:
Wxo comes from Edom, with His robes
From Bozrah crimson grained
It is the Lord, Who quits the fight;
His robes with blood are stained.

For us, O Christ, that war was waged
For us that Blood was spilt
For us Thy vest was purple dyed,
While washing out our guilt.

May we in Thine affliction mourn,
As Thou hast mourned in ours!
May we attend Thee in the pangs
Of Thy forsaken hours!

For Thou the winepress once didst tread,
Weighed down by bitter throes
The callous people saw the strife,
And left Thee to Thy woes.

Our stony heart O take away,
A tender spirit shed,
To weep for Thee, Who wept for us,
To bleed, since Thou hast bled.

Grant us the bliss of Thy redeemed,
To lean upon Thy breast
The Angel of Thy Presence send,
And take us to Thy rest.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: OR! is it nongnt to you that tread
verses:
OR! is it nongnt to you that tread
Along this path of sighs and woes,
To see a weary, guiltless Head
A mark for angry, taunting foes?

His back receives the cruel blow;
The pleughers score their furrows long
Scant pity do the smiters know:
His Fiame is weak, their arms are strong.

Why, bleeding Lamp ? why wounded thus?
Was ever sorrow like to Trine?
Oh! 'tis Thy Fatier's love to us,
That pours on Thee His wrath divine.

Though angels weep, they start not up;
Thou cravest succour; there is none:
“My Father, take away this cup!
Yet not My will, but Thine be done!”

While thus we share Thy bitter pangs,
In all Thy travails sore distrest,
In hope on Thee our spirit hangs
To reach with Thee our Easter rest.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

verses:
nf O mouvRN, thou rigid stone!

Victim to love sublime!
To love, with piercing throe!
He dies! oh, cruel crime!
Dark spectacle of woe!
What heart could e'er conceive the thought?
For mortals God to death is brought!

Your tears, mine eyes, begin!

Beweep my grievous sin,
The cause of woe so great:
The mercy of that love an? grief

What force of love there glows

pres. Then soften, Lord, our rocky heart,
And fervent love for Thee impart.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: ACCORDING to Thy gracious word
verses:
ACCORDING to Thy gracious word.
In meek humility.
This will I do, my dying Lord,
P I will remember Thee.

Thy Body, broken for my sake.
My Bread from Ileav:n shall be;
Thy testamental cup I take
And thus remember Thee.

Gethsemane can I forget,
Or there Thy conflict see,
Thine agony and bloody sweat
And not remember Thee?

When to the Cross I turn mine eyes,
Aud rest on Calvary,
O Lamb of God, my sacrifice!
I mnst remember Thee.

Remember Thee, and all Thy pains,
And all Thy love to me;
Yes, while a breath, a pulse remains,
Will I remember Thee

And when these failing lips grow dumb,
And mind and memory flee,
Vhen Thou shalt in Thy Kingdom come.
JEsus, remember me!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Life, and health, and peace possessin
verses:
Life, and health, and peace possessin
From the sinner's dying Friend

Were I'll sit, for ever viewing
Mercy's streams in streams of blo: d
Precious drops, my soul bedewing,
Plead and claim my peace with God

Jove and grief my heart dividin
With my tears His feet I'll bathe;
Constant still, in faith abiding,
Life deriving from His death

When I see Divine compassion,
Floating in His languid eye.

Here it is I find my heaven,
While upon the Lamb I gaze;
Loving much for much forgiven,
Ever resting on His grace
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Go to dark Gethsemane
verses:
See Him at the Judgment-hall,
Beaten, bound. reviled, arraigned
Mark Him meekly bearing all!
Mark the pangs His soul su-tained!
Shun not suffering, shame, or loss;
Learn of Cuxist to bear the Cross,

Thee the Lord of Glory see,
Made a sacrifice for you,
lbying on th' accurséd Tree:

Curis is ris'n! He seeks the skies:

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The Cross, upraised on Calvary's height
verses:
The Cross, upraised on Calvary's height,
The dead RepEEMER's bier,
From which the sun withdrew his light,
And hid him as in fear,
Ne'er, Lord, cn us shall darkly frown,
For now it shines in mercy down.

The Marys, round that sacred Wood,
Dissolved in bitter grief,
Dejected. br. ken-hearted, stood,

So kneel we, sunk in sorrow there:
Do Thou each kneeling sinner spare.

cres. We cling to that atoning Tree,
Whence we had g ne astray,

Thy precious Blood, of nameless price,

Then loathe thyself. disown thy deeds,

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: My God, I love Thee, yet my love
verses:
My God, I love Thee, yet my love
Springs not from hope of bliss above,
Nor since, who love Thee not, in ire,
Are punished with eternal fire.

O Jesu, Thou hast on the Tree
In all my guilt embraced me,
For me hast borne the nails, the spear,
Unmeasured scorn, the burning tear.

Thou hast endured unnumbered woe:,
The sweat of blood, the thorns, thethroes,
Yea, death itself, and all for me,
That I, a sinner, might be free.

Then why should I not love Thee well
Thy wondrous love no lip can tell!
It tills the earth, it gilds the skies,
It melts the heart, it never dies.

*Tis not for sake of heavenly joy,
Nor fearing Thou shouldst me destroy:
Not drawn by any hoped reward,
That I would love Thee, gracious Lord

But 'tis that Thou first lovedst me,
That I with all my soul love Thee,
And will love Thee, love Thee alone,
My Kise, my God, my very own.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Wnrex I survey the wondrous Cross
verses:
Wnrex I survey the wondrous Cross,
Qn which the Prrxcge of Glory died,
My richest gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.

Forbid it, Lord, that I should boast.
Save in the death of Christ, my God:
All those vain things, that chann me most,
I sacrifice them to His blood.

Behold His head, His hands, His feet!
Flow love and sorrow miugled donn!
Did e'er such love and sorrow mect,

Were all the realm of nature mine,
That were a present far too sma!l;
