hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O'ERWHELMED beneath a load of grief
verses:
O'ERWHELMED beneath a load of grief,
With eruel scorn assailed,
Our dear REDEEMER on the Cross,
In bitter pain is nailed.
Sore wounded, from His hands and fect
Outflows a fount of blood!
His face, His limbs, His breast, are
steeped O bathe them with a flood of tears,
In that most sacred flood.

He weeps, He prays, He groans, He dies!
His Mother's strieken heart
A ruthless sword hath deeply piereed,
With agonizing smart.
The graves are opened, rocks are rent;
The land, the ocean shake;
The temple's veil is torn in twain:
All hear the ery, and quake.

Thou, Sacrifice of deathless love,
To wash the sinner white,
Hast, by Thy life-imparting blood,
Made us the sons of light.
Then, JEsu, be our peace and joy,
Our life, our precious prize;
Our lamp to lead us on the path,
Our crown above the skies.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: WE sing the praise of Him who died
verses:
Inscribed upon the Cross, we see
The shining letters, ''God is love
He bears our sins upon the Tree;
He brings us mercy from above.

The balm of life, the cure of woe,
The measure and the pledge of love;
The sinner's refuge here below,
The angels' theme in heaven above,

It makes the coward spirit brave,
And nerves the feeb.e arm for fight;
It takes its terror from the grave,
And gilds the bed of death with light.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Atas! and did my Saviour bleed
verses:
Atas! and did my Saviour bleed?
And did my Sovereign die?
Would He devote that sacred Head
For such a worm as 1?

Was it for crimes that I had done,
He groaned upon the Tree?
Amazing pity! grace unknown!
And love beyond degree!

But crops of grief can ne'er repay
The debt of love I owe:
Here, Lord, I give myself away:
din 'Tis all that I can do.

The sun might well in darkness hide,
And sbnt his glories in,
When Christ, the mighty Maker, died
For mau, the creature's sin!

Thus might I hide my blushing face,
While His dear Cross appears
Dissolve my heart in thankfulness,
And melt my eyes in tears.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Norall the blood of beasts
verses:
Norall the blood of beasts,
On Jewish altars slain,
Could give the guilty conscience peace,
Or wash away the stain.

But Cunist, the heavenly Laxs,
Takes all our sins away;
A sacrifice of nobler name,
And richer blood than they.

P My faith would lay her hand
On that dear Head of Thine,
While, humble penitent, I stand,
And there confess my sin.

My soul looks back to see
The burdens Thou didst bear,
When hanging on the curséd Tree,
And hopes her guilt was there.

JF Lost sinners, we rejoice
To see the curse remove;
We bless the Laas with cheerful voice,
And sing His bleeding love.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Hare! the voice of love and mercy
verses:
Hare! the voice of love and mercy
Sounds aloud from Calvary
See! it rends the rocks in sucder,
Shakes the earth, and veils the sky
“Tc is finished!”
Hear the dying Savior cry.

'“Itis finished!” Oh! what joyance

Heavenly blessings, without measure,

“Tis finished

Saints, from hence your comfort draw

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Grory! glory! Lord, to Thee
verses:
Grory! glory! Lord, to Thee,
Who for us upon the Tree
Didst, amid the sharpe-t pains,

JeEsu's blood, with merit rife,
Flows. the soul's immortal life
Blessed be His gracious love,
Pas-iug all below, above!

Evermore the song we raise
This, His precious blood we praise
Which redeemed from endless pain
Sinners, held in Death's domain.

See the blood of Abel rise,
Claiming vengeance from the skies
JESO's blood, our ble-t release,
Pleads fur mercy, pardon, peace

When its praise, exalted high.
Ring. through earth, and mounts the sky,
H-aven rejoices, trembles Hell.
Sinking 'neath its broken spell

Let us, then, in concert sing!
Every earnest power bring!
Chanting this thrice-glorious flood!
JESU's ever sacred blood!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: For ever here my rest shall be
verses:
For ever here my rest shall be,
Close by Thy bleeding side;
This all my hope, and ail my plea
For me the Saviour died.

My dying Saviour, and my God,
'Thou Fount for guilt and sin,
Me ever sprinkle with Thy blood,
And cleanse, and keep me clean

O wash me, make me thus Thine Own;
O wash me! mine Thou art
O wash me! not my feet alone,
My hands, my head, my heart.

Th' atonement of Thy blood apply,
Till faith to sight improve

And all my soul be love.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: All is o'er; the pain, the sorrow
verses:
All is o'er; the pain, the sorrow,
Human taunts, and fiendish spite
Death shall be despoiled to-morrow
Of the prey he grasps to-night;
Yet once more to seal his doom,
CHRIST must sleep within the tomb.

Close and still the cell that holds Him,
While in brief repose He lies;
Deep the slumber that enfolds Him,
Veiled awhile from mortal eyes
Slumber such as needs must be
After hard-won victory

Fierce and deadly was the anguish,
Which on y onder Cross He bore; 8
How did soul and body languish,
Till the toil of death was o'er!
JF But that toil, so fierce and dread,

All night long, with plaintive voicing,
Chant His requiem soft and low;
eres, Loftier strains of loud rejoicing
From to-morrow's harps shall flow:

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

verses:

Sleeps His Form, from head to feet

Lying in the rock alone,
Hid beneath the seatéd stone.

Late that mournful eve was seen,
Spent with watch the Magdalene;
Early morn beheld her rise,
Wending on, with tearful eyes,
Towards the holy garden glade,
Where her buried Lord was laid.

So with Thee. till life shall end,
T would solemn vigil spend:
Let ine hew Thee, LorpD a shrine
In this rocky heart of mine,
Where, in pure embalméd cell
None but Thou may ever dwell.

Myrrh and spices will I bring,

Close the door from sight and sound
Of the busy wor d around;
And in patient watch remain,
Till my Lord appear again.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Easter-pary is here, and we
verses:
Easter-pary is here, and we
To our JEsus bow the knee;
Easter-day with joy is come
To the tenants of the tomb.

Death, and Hell, and shades of night,
Cannot hold the Lord of light;
Our great CapTarx triumphs well,
He hath burst the bars of Hell.

Death and Hell are desolate
Shattered is the brazen gate;
Broken are the bonds of death,
For our Jesus triumpheth.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Cunist the Lord is risen to-day
verses:
Cunist the Lord is risen to-day
Sons of men and angels say:
Raise your joys and triumphs high,
Sing, ye heavens, and earth reply.

Love's redeeming work is done,
Fought the fight, the battle won;
Lo! our Sun's eclipse is o'er!
Lo! He sets in blood no more.

Vain the stone, the watch, the seai;
Christ hath burst the gates of hell!
Death in vain forbids His rise,
Christ hath opened Paradise,

Lives again our glorious King;
Where, O Death, is now thy sting?
Once He died, our souls to save:
Where, thy victory, O grave?

Hail the Lord of earth and heaven!
Praise to Thee by both be given!
Thee we greet triumphant now!
Hail, the Resurrection Thou!

0 King of Glory! Soul of Bliss!
Everlasting life is this;
Thee to know, Thy pow'r to prove
Thus to sing, and thus to love!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The happy morn is come
verses:
What foe on us shall lay
The charge of sin ana guilt?
All sin is done away,
Since His rich blood was spilt:
Captivity is captive led,
Since Jusvus liveth that was dead.

Lo! sinners now can dare
To God to venture near;
Now Justice must declare
No cuuse remains for fear:
TS Captivity is captive led,
Since Jesus liveth that was dead.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: He is risen! He is risen
verses:
He is risen! He is risen!
Tell it with a joyful voice!
He has burst His three days' prison,
Let the whole wide earth rejoice:
JF Death is conquered, man is free,
Christ has won the victory.

Come, ye sad and fearful-hearted,
Smiling, glad, with radiant brow;
Lent's long shadows have departed,
All His woes are over now:
All the passion that He bore,
Sin and pain, can vex no more.

Come, with high and holy hymning,
Chant our Lord's triumphant lay
Not ene darksome c'oud is dimming
Yonder glorious morning ray,
Breaking o'er the purple East;
Brighter far our Easter feast.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Acary the Lord of Life and Light
verses:
Acary the Lord of Life and Light
Awakes the kindling ray,
Unseals the eyelids of the morn,
And pours increasing day.
Oh! what a night was that, which wrapt
The heathen world in gloom!
Ob! what a Sun, which broke this day,
Triumphant from the tomb!

Ten thousand diff'ting lips shall joiu
To hail this welcome morn,
Which scatters blessings from its wings
To nations yet unborn.

The pow''rs of darkness leegued in vain
To bind His soul in death;
He shook their kingdom when He fe!l
With His expiring breath.
And still for erring, guilty man
A Brother's pity flows
And still His bleeding heart is touched
With mem'ry of our woes.

if To Thee, my Savrocr, and my King,
Glad homage let me give,
And stand prepared like Thee to die,
With Thee that I may live!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Come once more, with songs descending
verses:
Come once more, with songs descending,
Angels, come our joy to share;
Lo! what pow'r the tomb is rending!
Free among Death's captives there, Lo! He leaves the Sepulchre!

Vain the Soldiers watching round Him,
Through the hours of darkness lone;
Vain the jealous care that bound Him
Deep within the sealéd stone:
Vain their madness!
All their toil is now undone.

If He will, with seals unbroken
He can leave the silent tomb:
Not more wondrous was the token,
At His birth first seen to come, When He issued
From the spotless Virgin's womb.

Lord, with Thee in daily dyin:
May we die, and with Thee rise,
Every earthly love denying,
May we lift to Thee our eyes,
Thee adoring,
y With our hearts above the skies.

my THE strife is o'er, the battle done
The victory of life is won;
The song of triumph has begun,
JF Alleluia!

The pow'rs of death have done their worst,
But Christ their legions hath dispersed
Let shout of holy joy outburst,

The three sad days are quickly sped
He rises glorious from the dead:
All glory to our risen Head

Lord! by the stripes which wounded Thee,
From Death's dread sting Thy servants free,
That we may live, and sing to Thee,
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: JF Jesus lives! no longer now
verses:
JF Jesus lives! no longer now
Can thy terrors, Death, appal us;
JESUS lives! by this we know
Thou, O Grave, canst not enthral us.
ff Alleluia!

Jesus lives! henceforth is death
But the gate of life immortal:
This shall calm our trembling breath,
When we pass its gloomy portal.

Jesus lives! for us He died;
Then, alone to JEsus living,
Pure in heart may we abide,
Glory to our Saviour giving.
ff Alleluia!

Jesus lives! our hearts know well
Nought from us His love shall sever:
JF Life, nor death, nor pow'rs of hell,

ff Alleluiat

JxEsus lives! to Him the throne

May we go where He is gone,

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord, in Thy name Thy servants plead
verses:
Lord, in Thy name Thy servants plead,
And Thou hast sworn to hear:
The harvest Thine, and Thine the seed,
The fresh and fading year.

Our hope, when Autumn winds blew wild,
We trusted, Lord, with Thee:
And still, now Spring has on us smiled,
We wait on Thy decree.

The former and the latter rain,
The Summer sun and air,
The green ear, and the golden grain,
All Thine, are our's by prayer.

Thine too by right, and our's by grace,
The wondrous growth unseen,
The hopes that soothe, the fears that brace,
The love that shines serene.

So grant the precious things brought forth
By sn and moon below,
That Thee in Thy new heaven and earth
We never may forego.

To Farner, Soy, and Hoty Ghost,
The God Whom we adore,
Be glory, as it was, is now,
And shall be evermore.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Son of Man, to Thee we cry
verses:
Son of Man, to Thee we cry:
By the wondrous mystery
Of Thy dwelling here on earth,
By Thy pure and holy birth,
Lord, Thy presence let us see!
Thou our Light and Saviour be!

Lamb of God, to Thee we cry:
By Thy bitter agony,
By Thy pangs to us unknown,
By Thy Spirit's parting groan,
cres, Lord, Thy presence let us see!
Thou our Light and Saviour bel

Prince of life, to Thee we cry:
By Thy glorious Majesty,
By Thy triumph o'er the grave,
By Thy pow'r to help and save,
Lord, Thy presence let us sce!
Thou our Light and Saviour be!

Lord of glory, God most high,
Man exalted to the sky,
With Thy love our bosom fill;
Hielp us to perform Thy will,
Then shall we Thy glory see,
Heaven our home, and we with Theo.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Christ, awhile to mortals given
verses:
Christ, awhile to mortals given,
Re-ascends His native Heaven.

There the glorious triumph waits
“Lift your heads, eternal gates!
Wide unfold the radiant scene
Take the Kine of Glory in!”

Him though highest Heaven receives,
Still He loves the earth He leaves
Though returning to Elis throne,
Still He calls mankind His Own

Near Himself prepares their place,
Saviour of the human race

Ever upward let us move,
Wafted on the wings of love
Looking when our Lord shall come,
Longing, panting after home
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Christ, Who, lifted to the sky
verses:
O Christ, Who, lifted to the sky.
Preparest us a seat on high
Sad exiles from the land above,
Oh! draw us home by cords of love
Of every good the Fountain, Lord,
Thou soon shalt be our rich reward

To match Thy people's briefest pain!
Our eyes unveiled, in blissful state,
Shall view Thee, Oh! how good! how great!

On Thee we ceaseless love shall pour
And Thee with ceaseless song adore
Thou ne'er dost quit a favoured race
In pledge of Thy redeeming grace,
O send Thy Spirit from Thy Throne,
To take and seal us for Thine Own,
Thou coming Judge of every tribe,
To Thee all praise do we ascribe,
Whom with the Father we adore,
And Hoty Sprrit everinore
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Ovr Lord is risen from the dead
verses:
Ovr Lord is risen from the dead,

and angels chant the solemn lay:

The Lord, that all His foes o'ercame,

“Who is the King of Glory ? Who?

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Rersorce! the Lord is King
verses:
Rersorce! the Lord is King,
Your Lord and Kiye adore!
Give thanks, ye mortals! sing!
And triumph evermore!
Sf Lift up your heart, lift up your voice;
Rejoice, again I say, rejoice!

Jeesvs the Saviovr reigns,
The God of truth and love:
When He had purged our stains,
He took His seat above:
Lift up your heart, lift up your voice;
Rejoice, again I say, rejoice!

Hesits at God's right hand,
Till all His foes submit,
And bow to His command,
And fall beneath His feet:
Lift up your heart, lift up your voice;
Rejoice, again I say, rejoice!

He all His foes shall quell,
Spall all our sins destroy,
And every bosom swell
With pure seraphic joy:
Lift up your heart, lift up your yolce,
Rejoice, again I say, rejoice!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: THE Head, that once was crowned with thorns
verses:
THE Head, that once was crowned with thorns,

Glory! glory to our King!

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

verses:

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Horry Ghost, with light divine

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Come, Hoty Guost, our souls inspire

hymns.title: Wen God of old came down from Heaven
verses:
Wen God of old came down from Heaven,
In power and wrath He came;
Before His feet the clouds were riven,
Half darkness and half flame.

But when He came the second time,
He came in power and love;
Softer than gale at morning prime,
Hovered His Holy Dove.

The fires, that rushed on Sinai down,
In sudden torrents dread,
Now gently light, a golden crown,
On every sainted head.

And, as on Israel's awe-struck ear
The Voice, exceeding loud,
The trump, that angels quake to hear,
Thrilled from the deep, dark cloud;

So, when the Spirit of our God
Came down, His flock to find,
A Voice from Heaven was heard abroad,
A rushing, mighty wind,

It fills the Church of God, it fills
The sinful wor'd around;
Only in stubborn hearts and wills
No place for it is found.

Come, Lord! come Wisdom b Love, and Power!
Open our ears to hear!
Let us not miss th' accepted hour;
Save, Lord, by love or fear.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Our blest RepEEMER, ere He breathed
verses:
Our blest RepEEMER, ere He breathed

A Guide, a Comforter, bequeathed
With us to dwell.

He came sweet influence to impart,
A gracious, willing Guest,
While He can find one humble heart
Wherein to rest.

And His that gentle voice we hear,
As soft as breath of even,
That checks each fault, that calms each fear,
And speaks of heaven.

And every virtue we possess,
And every vict'ry won,

Are His alone.

Thou Source of purity and grace,
Our weakness pitying sce

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Come, Thou Hoty Spiriv, nigh
verses:
Come, Thou Hoty Spiriv, nigh

Thou, of Comforters the best,

Softener of the sultry heat,
Solace "mid the tear!

Ever blessed, ever bright,

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

verses:
Come, aid and holy Dove

verses:

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

verses:

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Gor, unseen, yet ever near
verses:
O Gor, unseen, yet ever near,
Thy Presence may we feel;
And, thus inspired by holy fear,
Before Thine altar kneel

Here may Thy faithful people know
The blessings of Thy love,
The streams that thro' the desert fiow,
The manna from above,

We come, obedient to Thy Word,

Our drink, His precious Blood.

Thus may we all Thy words obey,
For we, O God, are Thine,
And go rejoicing on our way,
Renewed with strength divine.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O God of mercy, God of might
verses:

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

verses:
Wake, my tongue, the myst'ry telling,
Jesu's glorious Body sing!
Hymn the Blood, all price excelling,

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: My God, and is Thy Table spread
verses:

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord Jesus, God of grace and love
verses:
Lord Jesus, God of grace and love,
Revealed on Calvary,

“This day remember Me.”

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: For mercies, countless as the sands
verses:
For mercies, countless as the sands,
Which daily I receive
From Jesus my REDEEMER's hands,
My soul. what canst thou give?

Alas! from such a heart as mine,
What can I bring Him forth?
My best is stained and dyed with sin;
My all is nothing worth.

Yet this acknowledgment I'll make
For all He has hestowed
Salvation's sacred cup I'll take,
And call upon my God

The best return from one like me,
So wretched and so poor,
Is from His gifts to draw a plea,
And ask Him still for more.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord, when before Thy throne we meet
verses:
Lord, when before Thy throne we meet,
Thy goodness to adore,
From heaven, th' eternal mercy seat,
On us Thy blessing pour,
And make our inmost souls to be
A habitation meet for Thee.

Thy Body, for our ransom given,
Thy Blood, in mercy shed
With this immortal food from heaven,
Lord, let our souls be fed:
And as we round Thine Altar kneel,
Help us Thy quickening grace to feel.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

verses:

So we, while battling here below,

verses:

To darkness here alone,

Thou art the Way, the Truth, the Life
To us the Father give;

So bring us all, released from care,
To tread the heavenly floor,
With Thy Own saintly brother there,
Aud blesxéd Philip, spotless pair,
Tosce Thee evermore
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Bricst ty did the light divine
verses:
Bricst ty did the light divine
From his words and actions shine,
Whom the Twelve, with love unblamed,
“Son of Consolation " named.

Full of peace and lively joy,
Sped he on his high employ
By his mild exhorting word,
Adding many to the Lord.

Blessed Spirit, Who didst call
Barnabas and holy Paul,
And didst them with gifts endue,
Mighty words and wisdom true;

Grant us, Lord of Life, to be,
By their pattern, full of Thee,
That beside them we may stand,
In that day, on Thy right hand

Glory be to God above,
Fountain of eternal love;
To the Fatheer, and the Sow,
And the Sprzit, THRez in One,
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lo! from the desert homes
verses:
Lo! from the desert homes,
Where he hath hid so long,
The new Elias comes,
In sterne-t wisdom strong
The voice that cries
Of Christ from high,
And judgment nigh,
From op'ning skies.

O God! with love's sweet might
Who dost anoint, and arm
Christ's soldiers for the fight.
With spells that shield from harm;
Thrice bless¢d THREE,
Heav'n's endless days
Shall sing Thy praise

Ye haughty mountains, bow
Your sky-aspiring heads;
Ye valleys. hiding low,
Lift up your gentle meads
Make His ways plain
Your King before,
For evermore
He comes to reign.

Let thy dread voice around,
Thou karbinger of Light,
On our dull ears still sound.
Lest here we sleep in night,
Till Judgment come,
And on our path
Shall burst the wrath,
And deathless doom.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: In weakness great, and strong in hidden might
verses:
In weakness great, and strong in hidden might,
Thy Peter, Lord, a star of living light,
Though oft obscured. and once eclipsed, his rays
Yet shine again with purer, brighter blaze.

To meet Thee, walking o'er the troubled waves,
In zeal he ylunged, but lost the faith that saves;
The stony depths would soon have been hts tomb,
Hadst Tnou not plucked him from the watery doom.

The Cock crew loud Thy warning in his ears;
At Thy sad look he ponred remorseful tears
By Satan sifted, prostrate 'neath his blast,
SF On Thee, the Rock, he stood a rock at last.

A trusty Shepherd for Thy sheep he stands,
The keys of pard'ning Heav'n within his hands;
The cross of pain he crimsons o'er with blood,
Undying witness raising from the flood.

When round us threatening waves in wrath arise,
Oh! may we fix on Thee unswerving eyes!
On Thee may all our cl nging hopes be stayed
Thy look be mercy, and Thine arm bring aid!

Grant we may love Thee with Thy Martyr's power,
In sorrow melted for each sinning hour;
With him, while guarded from his mournful fall,
Confess Thee Cunist, aud win Thee Lord of all
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: As Jamesthe Great, with glowing zeal
verses:
As Jamesthe Great, with glowing zeal,
Unheeding smile or frown,
Relinquished all his earthly weal,
To win a brighter crown:
So, Lord, we haste, the world dis-

To follow Thee with faith unfeigned,
And draw Thy mercy down,

Should we for Thee to wrath be moved,
Disturbed by wild unrest,
Though thinking then Thou most wert

That then we served Thee best;
Oh! let Thy Spreir drop its balm,
To quell the storm, and shed a calm
On our unruly breast.

Though it were e'en to die;
cres, That he might rank on Thy right hand,
And there before the angels stand,
Thy favoured saint on high.

We from the Cross seek no retreat,
But, guided by Thy grace,
We crave to sit beneath Thy feet;
Right royal is the place!
JF So we may ever be Thine Own,
Where'er we view Thee stands a
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: BENEATM the fig-tree's grateful shade
verses:
BENEATM the fig-tree's grateful shade
Behoki the good Nathaniel lid.
Concealet from distaut eye:
But where is vision blind, or fa'nt,
To Ilim who saw the resting Saint
From far, yet ever nigh

The Nazareth, which he disdained,
And many a scornful tongue profaned,
Now beams a city bright;
As Thou, O Lord, on him dost ehine,
The N:zarcne stands forth divine,
A Kung before his sight!

The angels rise, the angels fal!,
They circle round the Lord of all:
This glory shall he view;
For guileless there he meekly stands,
In child-like faith at Jesu's hands,
Nathaniel, trnstful, true.

Lord, grant to us to be sincere,
With simp'e heart, and conscience clear
With truth to shine around;
That we may win the heavenly meed,
“Behold an Israelite indeed,
In whom no guile is found!”

pcres Then lead us to that vision bright,
Where stand the angel-hosts of light,
Fair stars in lustrous ring;
That, joining their immortal lays,
We ever may confess, and praise
Jt Our Savrour, God, and Kiva.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lo! sea and land their gifts outpour
verses:
Lo! sea and land their gifts outpour,
A tribute from their richest store,
To lie at Levi's feet
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: But we are still in fetters held
verses:
But we are still in fetters held,
By worldly charms and lucre spelie 1,
Our hearts all dead and col4;
Unyielding to the cries of grace,
With wills too weak to seek Thy face,
Fast bound in Satan's hold:
I “Come, follow Me!”
P Ah! how are we
To burst the chains of gold?

Thou hadst not where to lay Thine head,
When Matthew, by Thy mercy led,
Sought Thee to be his Guest;
But we, O Lord, of Thee have need,
Ou Thy rich bounty we must feed,
And lean upon Thy breast:
Then, follow Me!”
We cling to Thee,
Our Riches, and our Rest!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: THEY come, Gov's messengers of love, p Blest Jesu, Thou, Whose groans and tears
verses:
THEY come, Gov's messengers of love, p Blest Jesu, Thou, Whose groans and tears
They come from realms of peace above,
From homes of never-fading light,
From blissful mansions ever bright.

But chiefly at its journey's end,
*Tis yours the spirit to befriend,
And whisper to the willing heart,
Christian soul, in peace depart.”

Have sanctified frail nature's fears,
To earth in bitter sorrow weighed,
Thou didst not scorn Thine angels' aid.

An angel-guard to us supply,
When on the bed of death we lie;
And by Thine Own Almighty pow'r,
O shield us in the last dread hour.

To God the Fatuer, God the Soy,
And God the Spirit, Turke in One,
From all above, and all below,
Let joyful praise unceasing flow.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: With me is Luke, alone of all
verses:
With me is Luke, alone of all,
So sadly mourned the aged Paul;
Frail Demas, his in Christian love,
Is dead to him and things above.

The worldhad shewn its specious face,
And lured him from the heavenly race;
He loves it, and without a throe
Can leave a martyr to his woe.

But Luke his toils and travels shares, mf Thy changeless love, we pray, impart
Companion dear of all his cares;
Love lighting up his tender brow,
eres, He could not leave the captive now.

Behold him constant, faithful stand,
With healing lip, and healing hand,
His suff'ring brother fain to tend,
Evangelist, Physician, Friend.

Lord, make us steadfast as Thy Saint,
That we may toil, and never faint,
That we may stand, and never fall,
Upheld by Thee, the Help of all.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: How blest the union, gracious Lord
verses:
How blest the union, gracious Lord,
Which beams throuzhout Thy holy Word,
_Avray from Thine Own Essence!
Oh! when shall all Thy Church be one?
That precious siga of heaven begun,
The foretaste of Thy Presence!

Yet while for this we deeply yearn,
Still may our souls with fealty burn,
Of truth still careful, tender!
Lest, sinking it, we Thee betray,
And so arrest that glorious day,
When Thou shalt reign in splendor.

SJ Thy kinsmen, Lord, to Thee most dear,
Blest Jude and Simon, ever near,
Stood partners in Thy trial:
Saint Simon, glowing bright with zeal,
Saint Jude, with loving heart to feel
That faintness was denial

If we should meet Thine open foes,
When Satan hath with stealthy blows
Of unbelief undone them,
O grant a spirit, born atove,
To guard Thy cause in words of love,
Till truth to Thee hath won them.

Then, Lord, Thy grace to us impart,
Inspire the zeal, infuse the heart,
And warm the weak endeavour,
That high and low, that age and youth,
United in Thy saving truth,
May all be Thine for ever!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: WHO are these, like stars appearing
verses:
WHO are these, like stars appearing,
These, before God's throne who stand
Each a golden crown is wearing:
Who are all this glorious band?
Alleluia! hark! they sing,
Praising loud their heavenly King.

Who are these of dazzling brightness,
These, in God's own truth arrayed,
Clad in robes of purest whiteness,
Robes, whose lustre ne'er shall fade,
Ne'er be touched by Time's rude hand
Whence come all this glorious band

These are they, who have contended
For their Saviouk's honour long,
Wrestling on till life was ended,
Following not the sinful throng:
I These, who well the fight sustained,
Triumph through the Laxs have gained.

These are they, whose hearts were riven,
Sore with woe and anguish tried,
Who in prayer full oft have striven
With the God they glorified
Now their pain and conflict o'er,
God has bid them weep no more.

These, like priests, have watched and waited,
Off'ring up to Cuerist their will,
Soul and body consecrated,
Day and night to serve Him still:
t Now, in God's most holy place,
Blest they stand before His Face.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: WHat are these in bright array
verses:
WHat are these in bright array,
This innamerable throng,
Round the altar night and day,
Hymning one triumphant song?
Worthy is the Lamb, once slain,
Blessing. honour, glory, power,
Wisdom, riches to obtain,
New dominion every hour.”

These through fiery trials trod;
These from great affliction came;
Now before the throne of God,
Sealed with His Almighty name,
Clad in raiment pure ani white,
Victor-palms in every hand,
Through their dear REDEEMER's might,
More than conquerors they stand.

Hunger, thirst, disease unknown,
On immortal fruits they feed:
Them the Lamb amidst the Throne
Shall to living fountains lead:
Joy and gladness banish sighs,
Perfect love dispels all fear,
And for ever from their eyes
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Happy saints, who dwell in light
verses:
O Happy saints, who dwell in light,
And walk with Jgsvs, clothed in white,
Safe landed on that peaceful shore,
Where pilgrims meet to part no more.

Released from sin, and toil, and grief,
Death was their gate to endless life;
An opened cage, to let them fly,
And build their happy nest on high.

And now they range the heavenly plains,
And sing their hymns in melting strains;
And now their souls begin to prove
The heights and depths of Jesvu's love.

He cheers them with eternal smile
They sing hosannas all the while,
Or, overwhelmed with rapture sweet,
dim, Sink down adoring at His feet.

Ah! Lord! with tardy steps I creep,
And sometimes sing, and sometimes weep;
Yet strip me of this house of clay,
And I will sing as loud as they.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord of the Church, we humbly pray
verses:
Lord of the Church, we humbly pray
For those who guide us in Thy way,
And speak Thy holy Word:
With love divine their hearts inspire,
And touch their lips with hallowed fire,
And needful grace afford!

Help them to preach the truth of God,
Redemption through the Saviour's Blood:
Nor let the Srrriv cease
On all the Church His gifts to shower;
To them a Messenger of power,
To us, of life and peace.

y So may they live to Thee alone;
Then hear the welcome word, '* Well donei”
And take their crown above:
Enter into their Master's joy,
And all eternity emplo:
In praise, and bliss, and love
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: How beauteous are their feet
verses:
How beauteous are their feet,
Who stand on Zion's hill!
Who bring salvation on their tongues,
And words of peace reveal!
How charming is their voice!
How sweet the tidings are!
Zion, see thy Saviour King!
He reigns and triumphs here!

How happy are our ears,
That hear this joyful sound,
Which kings and prophets waited for,
And sought, but never found!
How blesséd are our eyes,
That see this heavenly light,
Which kings and prophets long desired,
But died without the sight.

The watchmen join their voice,
And tuneful notes employ
Jerusa'em breaks forth in songs,
And deserts learn the joy,
The Lord makes bare His Arm
Through all the earth abroad
Let every nation now behold
Their Saviour and their God.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Pour out Thy Spirit from on high
verses:
Pour out Thy Spirit from on high
Lord, Thine assembled servants bless
Thy grace and gifts to each supply,
And clothe Thy priests with righteous-

Within Thy temple when they stand
To teach the truth as taught by Thee,
O Lord, Jike stars in Thy right hand,
The Shepherds of the Churches be!

Then, when their work is finished here,
And they in hope their charge resign,
When Thou, Chief Shepherd, shalt appear,
May they, and we, and all be Thine!

With zeal and wisdom, faith impart,
With firmness, meekness from above,
To bear Thy people on their heart,
And love the souls whom Thou dost

To watch, and pray, and never faint,
By day and night strict guard to keep,
To warn the sinner, cheer the saint,
To nurse Thy lambs, and feed Thy sheep.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: How beautiful the feet that bring
verses:
How beautiful the feet that bring
The gladsome tidings here!
What gracious messengers e'en now
To our blest eyes appear

Thy servants speak; Thou only canst
The hearing ear bestow;
They smite the rock, but Thou alone
Dost bid the waters flow.

Bless we our God, Who grants us here
To sing in Sion's ways!
Oh! when, on heavenly Sion's hill,
When shall we sing Thy praise

They seek, but only Thou hast skill
To bring lost wand'rers home;
They call, but 'tis Thy love compels,
And then th' invited come.

Lord, Thou art with them of a truth,
Lest we should go astray
The twelve bright banners go before,
And shew us Canaan's way.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Saviour, Who Thy flock art feeding
verses:
Saviour, Who Thy flock art feeding,
With the shepherd's kindest care,
All the feeble gently leading,
While the lambs Thy bosom share;

Now, these little ones receiving,
Fold them in Thy gracious Arm
There, we know, Thy word believing,
Only there secure from harm!

Never, from Thy pasture roving,
Let them be the lion's prey;
Let Thy tenderness, so loving,
Keep them all life's dang'rous way

Then, within Thy fold eternal,
Let them find a resting- place,
Feed in pastures ever vernal,
Drink the rivers of Thy grace!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Iv token that thou shalt not fear
verses:
Iv token that thou shalt not fear
Christ crucified to own,
We print the Cross upon thee here,
And stamp thee His alone.

In token that thou shalt not blush
To glory in His Name,
We blazon here upon thy frout
His glory and His shame.

Thus, outwardly and visibly.
We seal thee for His Own;
And may the brow, that wears His cross,
Hereafter share His crown!

In token that thou shalt not flinch
HRIST'S quarrel! to maintain,
But 'neath His banner manfully
Firm at thy post remain

In token that thou too shalt tread
The path He travelled by,
Endure the Cross, despise the shame,
And sit thee down on high
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: And put your armour on
verses:
And put your armour on,
Strong in the strength which God supplies,
Through His eternal Sox.

Strong in the Lord of hosts,
And in His mighty power;
Who in the strength of Jesus trusts,
Is more than conqueror.

Stand, then, in His great might.
With all His strength endued
Bat take, to arm you in the fight,
The panoply of God.

That having all things done,
And all your conflicts passed,
Ye may o'ercome, through Christ alone,
And stand entire at last.

From strength to strength go on.
And wrestle. fight, and pray
Tread all the powers of darkness down,
And win the well-fought day!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O God, in Whose all-searching eye
verses:
O God, in Whose all-searching eye
Thy servants stand, to ratify
The vow baptismal by them made,
When first Thy hand was on them laid;
cres, Bless them, O holy Fatheer, bless,
Who Thee with heart and voice confess
May they, acknowledged as Thine Own,
Stand evermore before Thy throne!

Arm these, Thy soldiers, mighty Lord,
With shield of faith, and Spirit's sword;
Forth to the battle may they go,
And boldly aght against the foe,
With banner of the Cross unfurled,
And by it overcome the world;
And so at last receive from Thee
The palm and crown of victory.

Come, ever blessed Sririt, come,
And make Thy servants' hearts Thy homo;
May each a living temple be,
Hallowed for ever, Lord, to Thee:
Enrich that temple's holy shrine
With sevenfold gifts of grace divine;
With wisdom, light, and knowledge bless,
Strength, counsel, fear, and godliness.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: WuHew fairest Eve in Eden rose
verses:
WuHew fairest Eve in Eden rose
From sleeping Adam's side,
Thou led'st her, Lord, Thy precious gift,
To Adam for a bride.

So now Thy handmaid here bestow
On this, Thy waiting son;
Unite them both in holy bonds,
A loving race to run.

Make Thou their home as Eden bright,
Like Eden in her bloom;
Let choicest flow'rs adorn their path,
And round them shed perfume

Thy Church Thou tenderly hast loved
And washed her pure and fair;
No stain, nor wrinkle wouldst Thou trace,
But gee all comely there.

Thus, fondly knitted, ne'er may they
Discern the faulty spot,
pores. Or else, with gentle hand, let fall
A veil to hide the blot.

High sanctity didst Thou impress
Upon the marriage-rite,
When Cana saw the flowing streams
Shine crimson in the light.

Yet, though that nuptial feast was graced
With store of mystic wine,
Thou still canst fill a spouseless heart,
That knows no love but Thine.

Lord, grant us all, or virgins pure,
Or blest with wedded love,
To view the heavenly Bridegroom's face
In Paradise above.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Earth to earth, and dust to dust
verses:
Like the seed in spring-time sown,
Like the leaves in autumn strown,
Low theee goodly frames must lie,
All our pomp and glory die;
Soon the spoiler seeks his prey,
Soon he bears us all away.

Yet the seed, upraised again,
Clothes with green the smiling plain;
Onward as the seasons move,
Leaves and blossoms deck the grove:
And shall we forgotten lie,
Lost for ever when we die?

pr Lord, from Nature's gloomy night
Turn we to the Gospel's light;
Thou didst triumph o'er the grave,
Thou wilt all Thy people save:
Ransomed by Thy Blood, the just
Rise immortal from the dust.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: From out the deep, O Lord, on Thee
verses:
From out the deep, O Lord, on Thee,
The trembling seamen cry aloud:
Thou sittest Sovereign of the sea,
And ridest high above the cloud.

The raging waters o'er them roll,
And leaden mists efface the sky;
The tempest awes their inmost soul:
Yetstorm is music, Thou but nigh.

O Lord, appease the angry wild;
O smooth the billow's swelling crest
As soft the cradle rocks the child,
So gently lull them all to rest.

When we repose in tranquil sleep,
And winds are whistling high and drear,
Oh! think of those who moan and weep,
And cry for help when none is near.

The night is dark, and fierce the fray!
How dread the loneness 'mid the wave}
Be with them, though they fail to pray,
And save them from a watery grave.

When calm shall glaze the ocean face,
Still teach them ever Thee to know
Thy tender mercy still to trace,
Still Thine in weal as well as woe.

Fanned ever by Thy wings of love,
On land or sea, on ship or shore,
O guide us all to Thee above,
Our peaceful Haven evermore.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Tov, Who bid'st the ocean deep
verses:
O Tov, Who bid'st the ocean deep
Its own appointed limits keep,
Thou, Who dost bind the restless wave,
Eternal Father, strong to save, O hear us, when we cry to Thee
For all in peril on the sea!

O Saviour! Whose Almighty word
The winds and waves submissive heard,
Who walkedst on the foaming deep,
And calm amid its rage did sleep;
O hear us, when we cry to Thee
For all in peril on the sea!

O Sacred Sprrit! Who didst brood
Upon the Chaos dark and rude;
Who bad'st its angry tumult cease,
And light diffused, and life, and peace; O hear us, when weary to Thee
For all in peril on the seal

O Trryity of love and power,
Our brethren shield in danger's hour;
From rock and tempest them defend
To safety's harbour them attend
And ever let there rise to Thee
Glad hymns of praise from land and sea!

Before JEHOVAH'S awful throne,
Ye nations bow with sacred joy;
Know ye the Lord is God alone,
He can create, and He destroy.

nf His sovereign pow'r, withont our aid,
Made us of clay, and formed us men;
And when like wand'ring sheep we strayed, Firm as a rock Thy truth shall stand,
He brought us to His fold again.

We'llcrowd Thy gates with thankfulsongs,
As high as heavn our voices raise:
And earth, with her ten thousand tongues,
Shall fill Thy courts with sounding praise.

#f Wide as the world is Thy command;
Vast as eternity Thy love:
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Jerusalem, my happy home
verses:
Jerusalem, my happy home,
Name ever dear to me!
When shall my labours have an end,
In joy, and peace, and thee

And pearly gates behold?
Thy bulwarks, with salvation strong.
And streets of shining gold?

There happier bowr's than Eden bloom,
Nor sin, nor sorrow know:
Best seats! through rude and stormy scenes
I onward preas to you.

Or feel at death di-may
TF've Canaan's goodly land in view,
And realms of endless dav.

Apostles, Martyrs, Prophets, there
Around my Saviotr stand:
And soon my friends in Carist below
Will join the glorious band.

Jernsslem, my happy home!
My sonl still pants for thee:
Then shall my labours have an end,
When I thy joys shall see.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O God of Hosts, the mighty Lord
verses:
O God of Hosts, the mighty Lord,
How lovely is the place,
Where Thou, enthroned in glory, shew'st
The brightness of Thy face!

My longing soul faints with desire
To view Thy blest abode;
My panting heart and flesh cry out
For Thee, the living God.

O Lord of Hosts, my Kine and God,
How highly blest are they,
Who in Thy temple always dwell,
And there Thy praise display

For in Thy courts one single day
'Tis better to attend,
Than, Lord, in any place besides,
A thousand days to spend.

Much rather in God's house will
The meanest office take,
Than in the wealthy tents of sin
My pompous dwelling make.

For God, Who is our Sun and Shield,
Will grace and glory give;
And no good thing will He withhold
From them that justly live.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Graciovs Spirit, Dove divine
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: nf Amip the various scenes of ills
verses:
nf Amip the various scenes of ills,
Each stroke some heavenly aim fulfils:
And canst thou murmur at thy God,
Whose sovereign love directs the rod?
If Heaven afflicts, wilt thou repine?
Each heartfelt comfort may be thine;
Comforts that shall o'er death prevail,
And journey with thee thro' the vale.
Tho' tempests drive thee from the shore,
And floods descend, and billows roar:

Tho' death appearin threat'ning form,
With Him thou canst defy the storm.
He near thee, in the darkest shade,
Thou nevermore shalt be afraid:
For where thy loving Lord is found,
A Paradise is blooming round.
O Saviour, smooth our rugged way,
And lead us to the realms of day,
To softer skies, aud brighter plains,
Where everlasting sunshine reigns.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: THE Lord my pasture shall prepare
verses:
When in the saltry glebe I faint,
Or on the thirsty mountain pant,
To fertile vales and dewy meads,
My weary, wand'ring steps He leads,
Where peaceful rivers, soft and slow,
Amid the verdant landscape flow.

Though in the paths of death I tread,
With gloomy horrors overspread,
My steadfast heart shall fear no ill,
For Thou, O Lord, art with me still;
Thy friendly crook shall give me aid,
And guide me through the dreadful shade,

Though in a bare and rugged way,
Through devious, lonely wilds I stray,
Thy bounty shall my wants beguile,
The barren wilderness shall smile,
With sudden greens and herbage crowned,
And streams shall murmur al} around.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Wues all Thy mercies, O my God
verses:
Wues all Thy mercies, O my God,
My rising soul surveys,
Transported with the view, I'm lost
In wonder, love, and praise.

Thy Providence my life sustained,
And all my wants redrest,
When in the silent womb I lay,
And hung upon the breast.

When worn with sickness, oft hast Thou
With health renewed my face;
And, when io sins and sorrow sunk,
Revived my soul with grace.

Ten thousand thousand precious gifts
My daily thanks employ;
Nor is the least, a cheerful heart,
That tastes those gifts with joy.

Through every period of my life
Thy goodness I'll pursue
And after death, in distant worlds,
The glorious theme renew.

Through all eternity to Thee
A joyful seng I'll raise
But O! eternity's too short
To utter all Thy praise.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: The spacious firmament on high
verses:
The spacious firmament on high,
With all the blue ethereal sky,
And spangled heav'ns, a shining frame,
Their great Original proclaim.
Th' unwearied sun, from day to day,
Does his CREATOR'S pow'r display,
And publishes to every Jand
The work of an Almighty hand.

P Soon as the evening shades prevail,
The moon takes up the wondrous tale,
And nightly to the list'ning earth
Repeats the story of her birth;
Whilst all the stars that round her burn,
And all the planets, in their turn,
Confirm the tidings as they roll,
And spread the truth from pole to pole.

What, though in solemn silence all
Move round the dark terrestrial ball;
What, though no real voice or sound
Amidst their radiant orbs be found;
In Reason's ear they all rejoice,
And utter forth a glorious voice,
For ever singing as they shine:
'The hand that made us is Divine.”
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord, see how swelling crowds arise
verses:
Lord, see how swelling crowds arise,
To wreck me thick arrayed!
Hear how the throng insultiug cries:
His God denies him aid!”
But, Lord, my castle Thou wilt stand,
A shield before me spread
My worship, Thou hast lent Thine hand,
To raise my drooping head.

My voice hath sought the Lord above:
He heard me in the still,
And sent an answer, winged with love,
From yooder holy hill.
I laid me down, and took my rest;
T raised me up again:
Thou wert a pillow for my breast,
A cordial for my pain.

JF I will not fear ten thousand foes,
That marshal haughty bands,
And ring me round in angered rows,
To whelm me 'neath their hands.
Up, Lord! my God, reveal Thy face,
Aud smite the foemen down:
Thine is the safety, and Thy Grace
Thy people's brightest crown.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: J Wuerthightheheavenlytemples'ands
verses:
J Wuerthightheheavenlytemples'ands
The house of God not made with hands,
A great High Priest our nature weara,
The Guardian of mankind appears.

He, Who for men in mercy stood.
And poured on earth His precious blood
Pursues in heaven His plan of Grace,
And lives to aid the human race.

Though now ascended up on high.
He bends on earth a brother's eye;
Partaker of the human name,
He knows the frailty of our frame.

A Suff'rer once, He yet retains
A tender pity for our pains
And still remembers in the skies
His tears, and agonies, and cries.

In every pang that rends the heart,
The Man of Sorrows had a part
He sympathises with our grief,
And sends the suff'rer sweet relief.

With boldness, therefore, at the throne
Let us make all our sorrows known,
And ask the aids of heavenly power,
To help us in the evil hour.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Saapow of a mighty rock
verses:
Saapow of a mighty rock
Stretching o'er a weary land
Hide me from the tempest's shock
Let me in Thy shelter stand!

When Thy Presence, O my God,
Brighter is than eye can see,
Shadow on the heavenward road
Let me find my shade in Thee

F Till the race of life be run,
Titl my soul in rest be laid
God of gods, Thou art my Sun
Son of God, be Thou my Shade!

W an life's —_ o'er me break,
Like a storm against the wall,
Let me find, for mercy's sake,
Shelter where Thy shadows fall,

Out of Thee are shades of death,
Weary ways, and hours unblest
Shadow of the Rock, beneath
Thee alone are joy and rest.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Much in sorrow, oft in woe
verses:
Much in sorrow, oft in woe,
Onward, Christians, onward go!
Fight the fight, and, worn with strife,
Steep with tears the Bread of Life.

Onward, Christians, onward go!
Join the war, and face the foe;
Faint not, much doth yet remain:
Dreary is the long campaign.

Shrink not, Christians! will ye yield?
Will ye quit the painful field
Will ye fiee in danger's hour?
Know ye not your Capra's power?

Onward then to battle move!
More than conqu'rors ye shall prove;
Though opposed by many a foe,
Christian soldiers, onward go!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: if Au people, that on earth do dwell
verses:
Know that the Lord is God indeed
Without our aid He did us make;
We are His flock, He doth us feed,
And for His sheep He doth us take.

Oh! enter then His gates with praise,
Approach with joy His courts nnto;
Praise, laud, and bless His Name always,
For it is seemly so to do.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Pass of glory, raiment bright
verses:
Pass of glory, raiment bright,
Crowns that never fade away,
Gird and deck the saints in light,
Priests, and kings, and conqu'rors they.

Yet the conqu'rors bring their palms
To the Lamb amidst the throne,
And proclaim in joyful psalms
Vict'ry through His Cross alone.

Kings for harps their crowns resign,
Crying, as they strike the chords,
'Take the kingdom, it is Thine,
Kine of kings, and Lord of lords!”

Round the Altar priests confess,
If their robes are white as snow,
'Twas the Saviour's righteousness,
And His blood that made them so.

They were mortal, too, like us:
Ah! when we, like them, must die,
May our souls, translated thus,
Triumph, reign, and shine on high!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: my THE Son of God goes forth to war
verses:
my THE Son of God goes forth to war,
A Kingly crown to gain;
His blood-red banner streams afar
Who follows in His train?
Who best can drink His cup of woe.
Triumphant over pain,
Who patient bears His Cross below,
He follows in His train.

A glorious band, the chosen few,
On whom the Spirit came
Twelve valiant saints, their hope they knew
And mocked the cross and flame
They met the tyravt's brandished steel.
The lion's gory mane;
They bowed their necks the death to feel
Who follows in their train?

A noble army, men and boys
The matron and the maid
Around the Saviour's throne rejoice
In robes of light arrayed.
They climbed the steep ascent of heaven,
Through peril, toil, and pain
O God! to us may grace be given.
To follow in their train!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: All glorious above
verses:
All glorious above:
O gratefully sing
His pow'r and His love;
Our Shield and Defender,
The Ancient of days,
Pavilioned in splendor,
And girded with praise.

O tell of His might,
O sing of His grace,
Whose robe is the light,
Whose canopy space;
His chariots of wrath
Deep thunder-clouds form,
And dark is His path
On the wings of the storm

Frail children of dust,
And feeble as frail,
In Thee do we trust,
Nor find Thee to fail:
Thy mercies how tender:
How firm to the end!
Our Maker, Defender,
REDEEMER and Friend!

O measureless Might!
Ineffable Love!
While angels delight
To hymn Thee above,
The humbler creation,
Though feeble their lays,
With true adoration
Shall lisp to Thy praise.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Hosayya to the living Lord
verses:
Hosayya to the living Lord!
Hosanna to th' incarnate Word
To Curisr, Creator, Savtove, King,
Let earth, let Heaven, Hosanns sing,
Hosanna in the highest!

O Saviove, with protecting care
Return to this Thy house of prayer,
Assembled in Thy sacred Name,
Where we Thy parting promise claim
Hosanna in the highest!

But, chiefest, in our cleanséd breast,
Eternal, bid Thy Sprert rest;
And make our secret sonl to be
A Temple pure, and worthy Thee.
Hosanna in the highest!

So, in the last and dreadful day,
When earth and Heaven shall melt away,
Thy flock. redeemed from sinful stain,
Shall swell the sound of praise again.
Hosanna in the highest!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Happy soul, thy days are ended
verses:
Happy soul, thy days are ended,
All thy mourning days below
Go, by angel guards attended,
To the sight of Jesus go!

Waiting to receive thy spirit,
Lo! the Saviour stands above;
Claims the purchase of His merit,
Reaches forth the crown of love.

Struggle through thy latest passion
To thy dear REDEEMER's breast,
To His uttermogt salvation,
To His everlasting rest!

For the joy He sets before thee
Bear a momentary pain;
Die! to live the life of glory!
Suffer! with thy Lord to reign!

Tuoxr for ever! God of love,
Hear us from Thy throne above;
Thine for ever may we be,
Here, and in eternity!

Thine for ever! Lord of life,
Shield us through our earthly strife;
Thou, the Life, the Truth, the Way,
Guide us to the realms of day.

Thine for ever! Oh, how blest
They who find in Thee their rest!

Saviour, Guardian, heavenly Friend,
O defend us to the end.

Thine for ever! Saviour, keep
These, Thy frail and trembling sheep
Safe alone beneath Thy care,
Let us all Thy goodness share.

Thine for ever! Thou our Guide,
All our wants by Thee supplied,
All our sins by Thee forgiven,
Lead us, Lord, from earth to heaven.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Tstxe th' Almighty pow'r of God
verses:
Tstxe th' Almighty pow'r of God,
That made the mountains rise,
That spread the flowing seas abroad,
And built the lofty skies.
I sing the wisdom that ordained
The sun to rule the day;
The moon shines full at His command,
And all the stars obey.

I sing the goodness of the Lord,
That filled the earth with food
He formed the creatures with His

And then pronounced them good.
Lord, how Thy wonders are displayed,
Where'er I turn my eye!
If I survey the ground I tread,
Or gaze upon the sky,

There's not a plant or flow'r below,
But makes Thy glories known;
And clouds arise and tempests blow,
By order from Thy throne.
Thy creatures, num'rous as they be,
Are subject to Thy care;
There's nota place where we can flee,
But God is present there.

With wrath in hell beneath
*Tis on His earth I stand or move,
And 'tis His air I breathe.
His hand is my perpetual guard
e keeps me with His eye:
Why should I then forget the Lord,
Who is for ever nigh?
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: AUt hail the pow'r of Jesu's Name
verses:
AUt hail the pow'r of Jesu's Name!
Let angels prostrate fall!
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lokp of all!

my Let high-born Seraphs tune the Ffre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face, Who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball!
Now, hail the strength of Israel's might,

nyf Crown Him, ye Martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call!
Extol the stem of Jesse's Rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel's chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him Who saves you by His grace,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David's line,
Whom David Lord did call;
The God incarnate, Man divine
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation's call,
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: My life's a shade, my days
verses:
My life's a shade, my days
Apace to death decline
My Lord is life, He'll raise
My dust again, e'en mine!

My peaceful grave shall keep
My bones till that sweet day,
I wake from my long sleep,
And leave my bed of clay.
Sweet truth, &c.

My Lord His angels shall
Their golden trumpets sound,
At whose most welcome call
My grave shall be unbound.
Sweet truth, &c.

I said sometimes with tears,
Ah me! I'm loth to die!
Lord, silence Thou these fears:
My life's with Thee on high.
Sweet truth, &c.

What means my trembling heart,
To be thus shy of death;
My life and I ne'er part,
Though I resign my breath.
Sweet truth,
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Ye boundless realms of joy
verses:
Ye boundless realms of joy,
Exalt your Maker's fame,
His praise your song employ
Above the starry frame;
Your voices raise,
Ye cherubim
And seraphim,
To sing His praise.

Thou moon, that rul'st the night,
And sun, that guid'st the day,
Ye glitt'ring stars of light,
To Him your homage pay;
I His praise declare,
Ye heavens above,
And clouds that move
In liquid air.

United zeal be shewn
His wondrous fame to raise,
Whose glorious Name alone
Deserves our endless praise,
Earth's utmost ends
His power obey
His glorious sway
The sky transcends.

His chosen saints to grace,
He sets them up on high,
And favours Israel's race,
Who still to Him are nigh,
I O therefore raise
Your grateful voice,
And still rejoice
The Lord to praise,
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Deathless principle, arise
verses:
Deathless principle, arise!
Soar, thou native of the skies!
Pearl of price, by Jesus bought.
To His glorious likeness wrought!

Lo, He beckons from on high!
Fearless to His Presence fly!
Thine the merit of His Blood;
Thine the righteousness of God.

Angels, joyful to attend,
Hovering round thy pillow, bend
Wait to catch the signal given,
And escort thee quick to Heaven.

Is thy earthly house distrest,
Willing to retain her guest?
'Tis not thou, but she, must die:
Fly, celestial tenant, fly!

Burst thy shackles, drop thy clay,
Sweetly breathe thyself away;
Singing. to thy crown remove,
Swift of wing, and fired with love.

Saints, in glory perfect made,
Wait thy passage through the shade:
Swiftly to their wish be given:
Kindle higher joy in Heaven!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord, in this Thy mercy's day
verses:
Lord, in this Thy mercy's day,
cres, Ere it pass for aye away,
On our knees we fall and pray.

Holy Jesu, grant us tears,
Fill us with heart-searchipg fears,
Ere that awful doom appears.

Lord, on us Thy Sprgit pour,
Kneeling lowly at the door,
Ere it close for evermore.

By Thy night of agony,
By Thy supplicating cry,
By Thy willinguess to die,

By Thy tears of bitter woe
For Jerusalem below,
Let us not Thy love forego.

ny Grant us 'neath Thy wings a place,
Lest we lose this day of grace,
Ere we shall behold Thy face.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O PRAISE ye the Lord
verses:
O PRAISE ye the Lord,
Prepare our glad voice,
His praise in the great
Assembly to sing;
In our great Creator
Let Israel rejoice,
And children of Sion
Be glad in their King.

By angels in heaven
Of every degree,
And saints upon earth,
All praise be addrest
To God in Three Persons,
One God ever blest;
As it has been, now is,
And always shall be.

Let them His great Name
Extol in the dance
With timbrel and harp
His praises express;
Who always takes pleasure
His saints to advance,
And with His salvation
The humble to bless,
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Waew at Thy footstool, Lord, I bend
verses:
Waew at Thy footstool, Lord, I bend,
And plead with Thee for mercy there,
Think of the sinner's dying Friend,
And for His sake receive my prayer.

O think not of my shame and guilt,
My thousand stains of deepest dye;
Think of the blood which JEsvts spilt,
And let that blood my pardon buy.

Think, Lord, how I am still Thy Own,
The trembling creature of Thy hand;
Think how my heart to sin is prone,
And what temptations round me stand.

O think upon Thy holy Word,
And every plighted promise there;
How prayer should evermore be heard,
And how Thy glory is, to spare.

O think not of my doubts and fears,
My strivings with Thy grace divine;
But think on Jesu's woes and tears,
And let His merits stand for mine.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Ere God had built the mountains
verses:
Ere God had built the mountains,
Or raised the fruitful hills
Before He filled the fountains,
That feed the running rills,
Brought forth from everlasting,
I, Wisdom, dwelt with Him,
In joyance never wasting,
And brightness never

When like an archéd dwelling,
He spread the skies abroad
And swathed about the swelling
Of ocean's mighty flood
He wrought by weight and measure
And I was with Him then:
Myself the Faruer's pleasure,
And Mine the sons of men.

Thus Wisdom's words discover
Thy glory and Thy grace,
Thou everlasting Lover
Of our unworthy race!
Thy gracious eye surveyed us,
Ere stars were hung above
In wisdom Thou hast made us,
And died for us in love.

And canst Thou be delighted
With creatures such as we,
Who, when we saw Thee, slighted,
And nailed Thee to a tree?
Unfathomable Wonder,
And Mystery divine!
The voice, that speaks in thunder,
Says, “Sinner, I am thine!”

Jesu, Lover of my soul,
Let me to Thy bosom fly,
While the nearer waters roll,
While the tempest still is high!
Hide me, O my Savionr, hide,

Other refuge have I none;
Hangs my helpless soul on Thee:
dim, Leave, ah! leave me not alone,
Still support and comfort me!
All my trust on Thee is stayed,
All my help from Thee I bring:
Cover my defenceless head
With the shadow of Thy wing!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O King of earth, and air, and sea
verses:
O King of earth, and air, and sea,
The hungry ravens cry to Thee:
To Thee the scaly tribes, that sweep
The bosom of the boundless deep

To Thee the lions roaring call,
The common Father, good to all!
Then grant Thy servants, Lord, we pray,
Our daily bread from day to day.

The fishes may for food complain
The ravens spread their wings in vain;
The roaring lions lack and ine
But, God, Thou carest still for Thine!

Thy bounteous hand with food can bless
The bleak and lonely wilderness:
And Thou hast taught us, Lord, to pray
For daily bread from day to day.

And oh! when through the wilds we roam,
That part us from our heavenly home;
When lost in danger, want, and woe,
Our faithless tears begin to flow,

Do Thou Thy gracious comfort give,
By which alone the soul may live
And grant Thy servants, Lord, we pray,
The bread of life from day to day.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O ALL ye people, clap your hands
verses:
Our bitter foemen He shall bruise.
And lay them low beneath our feet;
A heritage for us shall choose
Great Jacob's shrine, His favoured seat.

The princes haste to Zion's rock,
The princes of our honoured race
Above His universal flock
God spreads the buckler of His grace.

God reigns supreme, the Lord of all;
With fervent heart repeat the cry!
Before His ark the heathen fall,
The throne of Majesty on high.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Hark, my soul! it is the Lord
verses:
Hark, my soul! it is the Lord,
*Tis thy Saviour, hear His word:
Jesus speaks, and speaks to thee:
“Say, poor sinner, lov'st thou Me?”

“T delivered thee when bound,
And, when bleeding, healed thy wound,
Sought thee wandering, set thee right,
Turned thy darkness into light.

Can a woman's tender care
Cease to guard the child she bare?
Yes, she may forgetful be;
Yet will I remember thee.

Mine is an unchanging love,
Higher than the heights above,
Deeper than the depths beneath.
Free and faithful, strong as death.

Lord, it is my chief complaint,
That my love is weak and faint;
Yet I luve Thee and adore!
Oh! for grace to love Thee more!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: God moves in a mysterious way
verses:
God moves in a mysterious way
His wonders to perform;
He plants His footsteps in the sea,
And rides upon the storm,

Deep in unfathomable mines
Ot never-failing skill.
He treasures up His bright designs,
And works His sovereign will.

Ye fearful saints, fresh conrage take
The clouds ye 80 much dread
Are big with mercy, and shall break
In blessings on your head.

Judge not the Lord by feeble sense,
But trust Him for His grace;
Behind a frowning providence
He hides a smiling face.

His purposes will ripen fast,
Unfolding every hour;
The bud may have a bitter taste,
But sweet will be the flower.

Blind unbelief is sure to err,
And scan His'work in vain 3
God is His Own Interpreter,
And He will make it plain.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: When gath'ring clouds around I view
verses:
When gath'ring clouds around I view,
And days are dark and friends are few,
ere3, On Him I lean, Who, not in vain,
Experienced every human pain
He sees my wants, allays my fears,
And counts and treasures up my tears.

If ought should tempt my soul to stray
From heavenly wisdom's narrow way
To fly the good I would pursue,
Or do the sin I would not do;
Still He, Who felt temptation's pow',
Shall guard me in that dang'rous hour.

If wounded love my bosom swell
Deceived by those I prized too well
He shail His pitying aid bestow,
Who felt on earth severer woe;
At once betrayed, denied, or fled,
By those who shared His daily bread.

If'vexing thoughts within me rise.
And, sore dismayed, my spirit dies
Still He, Who once vouchsafed to bear
An anguish bord'ring on despair,
Shall sweetly soothe, shall gently dry
The throbbing heart, the streaming eye

And O! when I have safely past
Through every conflict but the last
Still, still unchanging, watch beside
My painful bed, for Thou hast died!
Then point to realms of cloudless day,
And wipe the latest tear away!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: As pants the hart for cooling streams
verses:
As pants the hart for cooling streams,
When heated in the chase;
So longs my soul, O God, for Thee,
And Thy refreshing grace.

For Thee, my God, the living God,
My thirsty soul doth pine:
Oh, when shall I behold Thy face,
Thou Majesty divine!

Why restless, why cast down, my soul?
Trust God, Who will employ
His aid for thee, and change thy sighs
To thankful hymns of joy.

My heart is pierced, as with a sword,
'Whilst thus my foes upbraid
Vain boaster! where is now Thy God?
And where His promised aid?

God of my strength, how long shall I,
Like one forgotten, mourn?
Forlorn, forsaken, and exposed
To my oppressors' scorn

Whyrestless, why cast down, my soul?
Hope still, and thou shalt sing
The praise of Him, who is thy God,
Thy health's eternal Spring.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord of mercy and of might
verses:
Lord of mercy and of might!
Of mankind the Life and Light!

Maker, Teacher Infinite!
P Jxsus! hear and save!
Who, when sin's tremendous doom
Gave creation to the tomb,

Didst not scorn the Virgin's womb,
P Jesus! hear and savet
Mighty Monarch! Saviour mild!
Humbled to a mortal Child,

Captive, beaten, bound, reviled,
P Jesus! hear and save!

Throned above celestial things,
Borne aloft on Angels' wings,
Lord of lords, and Kine of kings,
Jesus! hear and save!

Who shalt yet return from high,
Robed in might and majesty,
Hear us! help us when we cry,
i? Jzsvus! hear and save!

Lord of power, Lord of might,
God and Farther of us all,

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

Than human eyes can know!

Cease not to watch and pray

verses:
Far from the world, O Lord, I flee,
From strife and tumult far
From scenes, where Satan wages still
His most successful war.

The calm retreat, the silent shade,
With prayer and praise agree,
And seem by Thy sweet bounty made
For those who follow Thee.

There, if Thy Spirit touch the soul,
And grace her mean abode,
With what delight, and peace, and love,
She communes with her God!

Her solitary lays:

Friend of the friendless and the faint,

hymns.title: My God and Fares, while I stray
verses:

Far from my home, on life's rough way,
O teach me from my heart to say,
Thy will be done.”

Though dark my path, and sad my lot,
Let me be still, and murmur not,

“Thy will be done.”

Submissive still would I reply,
'Thy will be done.”

verses:
OH! happy feet that tread
Thine earthly courts, O Lord!

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Wuy storm the heathen? Wherefore do they ring
verses:
Wuy storm the heathen? Wherefore do they ring
The frantic outcry, to depose my King?

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Clothed with state, and girt with might
verses:
Clothed with state, and girt with might,

Stronger art Thou, Lord of skies:
Firm and true Thy promise lies,

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

verses:

Shall chase the gloom away.

That gift for us hast Thou reserved,
That day of shining Grace,
Of which the sun, in lustrous sheen,
Scarce shadows forth a trace,

Shall mount upon the wing,

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

In the glorious, golden city,

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Lord, how excellent Thy Name
verses:
O Lord, how excellent Thy Name!
It sounds aloud from pole to pole!
Thy glory soars above this frame
The heavens beneath it humbly roll.

The son of man, to win Thy grace?

Sweet Spirit, comfort me

hymns.title: O Hope of mourners, sad and meek

hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: BRIEF life is here our portion
verses:

Brief sorrow, short-lived care;
The life that knows no ending,
The tearless life is there.

For mortals, and for sinners,
