And Spreir, ever Holy!
To Heav'n's immortal throne
Uplift your praise, ye lowly
The great THRER-One adore!
Exalt His mighty Name!
Who was, is now, shall be
Eternally the same!

ErERNat beam of Light divine,
Thou Fount of unexhausted love,
In Whom the Father's glories shine
Through earth beneath and Heaven

O Jesu! weary wanderers' rest!
Give me Thy easy yoke to bear;
With steadfast patience arm my breast, Thy pow'r my strength and fortress is,
With spotless love, and lowly fear.

I thankful take the cup from Thee,
Prepared and mingled by Thy skill:
Though bitter to the taste it be,
'Tis strong the wounded soul to heal.

BE Thou, O Rock of Ages, nigh!
Each murm'ring thought shall then
be gone,
JF And grief, and fear, and care shall fly,
As clouds before the mid-day sun.

Oh! speak my warring passions peace,
And bid my trembling heart “Be still!”

O Death, whereis thy sting ? Where now
Thy boasted victory, O Grave?
Who dares contend with God, or who
Can hurt whom God delights to save
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: My epirit longs for Thee
verses:
My epirit longs for Thee
Within my troubled breast,
Though I unworthy be
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Our God stands firm, a rock and tow'r
verses:
Our God stands firm, a rock and tow'r,
A shield when danger presses;
A ready he!lp in every hour,
When doubt or pain distresses!
For our malignant Foe
Unswerving aims his blow;
His fearful arms the while,
Dark pow'r and darker guile:
His hidden craft is matchless.

Our strength is weakness in the fight
ur courage soon defection:
But comes a Warrior, clad in might,
A Prince of God's election
Who is this wondrous Chief,
That brings this glad relief
The field of battle boasts
Christ Jesus, Lor of Hosts,
Still conq'ring and to conquer!

Then, Lord, arise! lift up Thine arm!
With mizhty succour stay us!
Oh! turn aside the deadly harm,
When Satan would betray us;
That rescued by Thy hand,
In triumph we may stand,
And round Thy footstool crowd,
In joy to sing aloud
2 High praise to our RepERMER!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: To God on high be thanks and praise
verses:
To God on high be thanks and praise
For mercy ceasing never,
Whereby no foe a hand can raise,
Nor harm can reach us ever!
With joy to Him our hearts ascend,
The Source of peace, that knows no end,
Apeace that none can sever!

The honours, paid Thy holy Name,
To hear Thou ever deignest!
Thou, God the Fatheer, still the same,
Unshaken ever reignest!
Unmeasured stands Thy glorious might
Thy thoughts, Thy deeds outstrip the light!
Our heaven Thou, Lord, remainest

Lord Jesu Christ, the only Son
Of God, the King supernal!
The life of sinners lost, undone,
The death of strifes infernal!
Immortal Lams, of heavenly race,
Our need supply, outpour Thy grace
On all, in love eternal!

O Holy Sprrit, Gift supreme!
Sweet Comforter, all-curing!
Those, whom their Savrour doth redeem
From death, and Hell's alluring,
Delivered through His mortal throes,
Save Thou from all their wasting woes,
Thine Own in trust enduring!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Love divine, all love excelling
verses:
Love divine, all love excelling,
Joy of heaven, to earth come down!
Fix in us Thy humble dwelling,
All Thy faithful mercies crown:
Jesu, Thou art all compassion,
Pure, unbounded Love Thou art;
Visit us with Thy salvation,
Enter every trembling heart.

Come, Almighty to deliver!
Let us all Thy life receive
Suddenly return. and never,
Never more Thy temples leave.
Thee we would be always blessing,
Serve Thee as Thy hosts above
Pray, and praise Thee, without ceasing,
Glory in Thy perfect love.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: My soul, there is a country
verses:
My soul, there is a country,
Afar beyond the stars,
Where stands a winged sentry,
All skilful in the wars;

And there "bove noise and danger,
Sweet Peace sits crowned with smiles;
And Ong, born in a manger,
Commands the beauteous files.

He thee hath ever friended,
And, Oh! my soul, awake!
He hath in love descended,
To die here for thy sake.

ny If thou canst get but thither,
There grows the flower of peace,
The rose that cannot wither,
Thy fortress and thy ease.

Leave, then, thy foolish ranges!
For none can thee secure,
But Ong, Who never changes,
Thy God, thy Life, thy Cure.

To Thee, O Lord,
Thine Own through life, in weal or woe;
If joy or trouble I inherit,
The joy from Thee doth ever flow
In trouble still Thy praise shall sound,
Till life shall reach its closing bound.

When all forlorn, despairing, weeping,
'What doth my anxious heart desire
It ever would be pleasure reaping,
By this, its torment, set afire:
The sin, O help me to suppress,
To love Thee more, sin ever less!

Thy will be done!” be my petiti.
When I my wants to Thee confide!
Ot grant me. with a meek submission,
Still wholly Thine, whate'er betide,
dm. In quiet trust to draw each breath,
Till these mine eyes shall sleep in 'death!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Saviour, Whom I fain would love
verses:
Saviour, Whom I fain would love,
Jesus, crucified for me,
Fix my roving heart above,
Draw me nearer unto Thee.
Thee to praise, and Thee to know,
Make the joy of saints below
Thee to see, and Thee to love,
Make the bliss of saints above.

Lor», it is not life to live,
Thy presence Thou deny:
Lord, if Thou Thy presence give,
"Tis no longer death to die.
JF Source and Giver of repese,
Only from Thy love it flows;
Peace and happiness are Thine,
Mine they are, if Thou art mine,
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Tsou, the true and only Light
verses:
O Tsou, the true and only Light,
Direct the souls that walk in night,
And bring them 'neath Thy shelt'ring

my Enlighten with Thy beams of grace
The souls that wander in their race
When marked for soft deceit a prey,
Still keep them safe within Thy way.

If haply they should lapse to sin,
Then let Thy voice be heard within!
Each wounded conscience help and heal, Shall here, and there, for ever raise
That heavenly joys it yet may feel!

Oh! may the deaf their ears unclose!
The dumb no longer speech oppose!
But learn from Thee, their Lord to bless,
Him, Whom their hearts must needs

So they with us, in bonds of love,
On earth, and in the realms above,
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Blest are the pure in heart
verses:
The Lord, Who left the sky,
Onur life and peace to bring,
And dwelt in lowliness with men,
Their Pattern and their King;

To God the Fatuer, Son,
And Sprgit glory be;
As 'twas, and is, and shall be so,
To all eternity.

Still to the lowly soul
He doth Himself impart
And for His dwelling, and His throne,
Chooseth the pure in heart.

Lord, we Thy presence seek
Our's may this blessing be;
O give the pure and lowly heart,
A temple meet for Thee.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Worp celestial, Who Thy rest
verses:
O Worp celestial, Who Thy rest
Hast quitted in the Father's breast,
Who, after lapse of ages born,
Hast come to aid a world forlorn;
Now light our bosoms from above,
And fire them with Thy warmest love,
That heavenly joys may fill the heart,
Where joys, that fade, no bliss impart;
That when the Judge shall, in His ire,
Consign the guilty to the fire,

And mercy's voice, with loving cry,
Shall claim the righteous for the sky
We ne'er, the food for flames, be tost
*Mid darkling storms that wreck the lost,
But, looking on Thy Face Divine,
May share the rays that ceaseless shine.
To God the Faruer, God the Son,
And Hoty Sprrit, THREE in ONg,
As ever giv'n, so give we still,
All praise, eternity to fill.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Far from my heavenly home
verses:
Far from my heavenly home,
Far from my Father's breast,
I fainting cry, blest Sprrit, come,
id speed me to my rest!

My spirit homeward turns,
And fain would thither flee
My heart, O Sion, droops and yearns,
When I remember thee.

To God the Fatheer, Soy,
And Spirit, glory be;
As 'twas, and is, and shall be so
To all eternity.

My God, my life, be near!
On Thee my hopes I cast:
O guide me through the desert here,
And bring me home at last!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: WHEN the dark waves round us roll
verses:
WHEN the dark waves round us roll,
And we look in vain for aid,
Speak, Lord, to the trembling soul,
'*¥tis I, be not afraid!”

When we dimly trace Thy form,
In mysterious clouds arrayed,
Be the echo of the storm,

When our brightest hopes depatt,
When our fairest visions fade,
Whisper to the fainting heart,
'*It is I, be not afraid!"

When we weep beside the bier,
Where some well-loved form is laid,
Oh! may then the mourner hear,
tis I, be not afraid!”

When with wearing hopeless pain,
Sinks the spirit, sore dismayed,
Breathe Thou then the comfort-strain,

When we feel the end is near,
Passing into death's dark shade,
May the voice be strong and clear,
we “Tt is I, be not afraid!”
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: My song is love unknown
verses:
My song is love unknown,
My Saviour's love to me;
Love to the loveless shewn,
That they might lovely be:
Oh! who am I,
That, for my sake,
My Lord should take
Frail flesh and die?

Why, what hath my Lord done?
What makes this rage and spite
He made the lame to run,
He gave the blind their sight:
Sweet injuries!
Yet they at these
Themselves displease,
And 'gainst Him rise!

In life no house, no home,
y Lord on earth might have:
In death no friendly tomb,
But what a stranger gave;
What may I say?
Heav'n was His home,
But mine the tomb,
Wherein He lay.

Here might I stay and sing;
No story so divine;
Never was love, dear Kine,
Never was grief like Thine!
t This is my Friend,
In Whose sweet praise,
Tall my days
Could gladly spend.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: CHRISTIAN, seek not yet repose
verses:
Gird thy heavenly armour on,
Wear it ever, night and day
Near thee lurks the evil One;
Therefore watch and pray.

Watch, for thou thy guard must keep:
Pray, for God must speed thy way:
Narrow is the road and:steep:
Therefore watch and pray.

Listen to thy sorrowing Lord,
Him thou lovest to obey;
It is He, Who speaks the word,
yp Therefore watch and pray.

'Twas by watching, and by prayer,
Holy men of olden da:
Won the palms and crowns they wear;
Therefore watch and pray.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Jesu, Lord, to me impart
verses:
Jesu, Lord, to me impart
Shelter in Thy wounded heart;
Let me ever here abide,
Resting in Thy stricken side.

If the Evil One with wiles,
If the world with wealth beguiles,
In Thy heart retreat is sure,
In Thy side I rest secure.

When the flesh, more wily, waits,
Haunting me with tempting baits,
Fearless I may safe abide,
All my refuge this Thy side.

When shall come my closing day,
JES, cast me not away!
Grant me Saviour, when I die,
Buried in Thy side to lie.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Broun a stranger at the door
verses:
Broun a stranger at the door!
He gently knocks, has knocked before,
Has waited long, is waiting still:
You treat no other friend so ill,

O lovely Visitor! He stands,
With melting heart and bleeding hands!
O matchless kindness, for He shows
This matchless kindness to His foes!

But will He prove my friend indeed
He will; the very friend you need;
The Friend of sinners! yes, 'tis He,
With garments dyed on Calvary.

Rise! touched with gratitude divine!
Turn out His enemy and thine.
That soul-destroying monster Sin,
And let the heavenly Stranger in!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Nearer, my God, to Thee!
verses:
Nearer, my God, to Thee!
Hear Thou my prayer;
E'en though a heavy cross
Fainting I bear,
Still all my prayer shall be;
Nearer, my God, to Thee
Nearer to Thee!”

If, where they led my Lord,
I too am borne,
Planting my steps in His,
Weary and worn;
May the path carry me
Nearer, my God, to Thee;
Nearer to Thee!”

If Thou the cup of pain
Givest to drink,
Let not my trembling lip
From the draught shrink;
So by my woes to be
“Nearer, my God, to Thee;
Nearer to Thee!”

Though the great battle rage
Hotly around,
Still where my Captain fights
Let me be found;
Through toils and strife to be
Nearer, my God, to Thee
Nearer to Thee lt”

When, my course finished,
Breathe my last breath,
Ent'ring the shadowy
Valley of death;
Even there shall I be
Nearer, my God, to Thee;
Nearer to Thee!”

And when, Thou, Lord, once more
Glorious shalt come,
Oh! for a dwelling-place,
In Thy bright home!
Through all eternity
'Nearer, my God, to Thee;
Nearer to Thee!”
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: ALuicuty God, Thy piercing Eye
verses:
ALuicuty God, Thy piercing Eye
Strikes through the shades of night,
And our most secret actions lie
All open to Thy sight.

There's not a sin that we commit
Nor wicked word we say,
But in Thy dreadful book 'tis writ
Against the judgment-day.

And must the crimes that I have done,
Be read and published there,
Be all exposed before the sun,
While men and angels hear

Lord! at Thy feet ashamed I lie,
I upward dare not look;
Forgive my sins before I die,
And blot them from Thy Book!

Remember all the dying pains
That my REDEEMER felt,
And let His blood wash out my stains,
And answer for my guilt.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O precious Saviour, from Thy throne
verses:
O precious Saviour, from Thy throne
Of starry splendor Thou hast flown,
Thy lost and ruined sheep to seek,
A Shepherd ever faithful, meek!
To Thy dear Self O draw Thou me,
That I may ever follow Thee!

Alas! how sadly fall'n am I!
A wand'rer from Thy fold I cry!
eres, O! save me from infernal pains,
And in Thy blood blot out my stains;
That, washed by Thee as white as snow,
My heart with love may ever glow.

O mourners' Comfort! souls' Delight!
Thou loving Fount of mercy bright!
Indulgent Saviour, nigh me stand,
To screen me from the foeman's hand!
Thou faithful Shepherd of the sheep,
Redeem me when in death I sleep.

9 Bridegroom, decked in rich array!
Outshining far the orb of day,
Still sweeter than the honied store,
Thy favour grant me I implore;
Forgiveness that I e'er have strayed,
And joy in dying, ne'er to fade!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Jost as I am, without one plea
verses:
Jost as I am, without one plea,
But that Thy blood was shed for me,
And that Thou bid'st me come to Thee,
O Lamb of God, I come!

Just as I am, and waiting not
To cleanse my soul of one dark blot,
To Thee, Whose blood can cleanse each
spot, p Because Thy promise I believe:
O Lamb of God, I come!

Just as I am, though tossed about
With many a conflict, many a doubt,
Fightings and fears within, without,
O Lamb of God, I come!

Just as I am, poor, wretched, blind,
Sight, riches, healing of the mind,
Yea, all I need, in Thee to find,
O Lamb of God, I come!

Just as Iam, Thou wilt receive,
Wilt welcome, pardon, cleanse,

Just as Iam: Thy love unknown
Has broken every barrier down:
Thine now to be, yea, Thine alone,
O Lamb of God, I come!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: My God, my Life, my mh
verses:
My God, my Life, my mh.
To Thee, to Thee J call:
I cannot live if Thou remove,
For Thou art all in all.

Thy shining grace can cheer
This dungeon where I dwell:
'Tis Paradise when Thou art here;
If Thou depart 'tis hell.

Nor earth, nor all the sky,
Can one delight afford
No, not a drop of real joy,
Without Thy Presence, Lord.

To Thee, and Thee alone,
The angels owe their bliss
They sit around Thy gracious throne,
And dwell where JEsvus is.

Not all the harps above
Can make a heavenly place,
If God His residence remove,
Or but conceal His face.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Sacrep Heap! now wounded
verses:
O Sacrep Heap! now wounded,
With grief and shame weighed down,
Now scornfully surrounded
With thorns, Thine only Crown!
O Sacrep Heap! What glory,
What bliss till now was Thine!
Yet, though despised and gory,
JS I joy to call Thee mine.

What Thou, my Lord, hast suffered
Was all for sinners' gain
Mine, mine was the transgression,
But Thine the deadly pain.
Lo! here I fall, my Saviorr!
"Tis I deserve Thy place;
Look on me with Thy favor,
Vouchsafe to me Thy grace.

The joy can ne'er be spoken,
Above all joys beside,
When in Thy Body broken
Ithus with safety bide.
Lord of my life, desiring
Thy glory now to see,
Beside Thy Cross expiring.
Td breathe my soul to Thee.

Be near me when I'm dying;
Oh! shew Thy Cross to me;
And to my succoar fiying,
_Come, Lord, and set me free!
When strength and comfort langaish
Amidst the final throe,
Release me from my anguish
By Thine Own pain and woe.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Come, my soul, thy suit prepare
verses:
Come, my soul, thy suit prepare
JEsus loves to aiswer prayer;
He Himself has bid thee pray,
Therefore will not say thee nay.

Thou art coming to a King,
Large petitions with thee bring
For His grace and pow'r are such,
None can ever ask too much.

With my burden I begin:
Lord, remove this load of sin;
Let Thy blood, for sinners spilt,
Set my conscience free from guilt

While I am a pilgrim here,
Let Thy love my spirit cheer;
As my Guide, my Guard, my Friend,
Lead me to my journey's end.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Mv faith looks up to Thee
verses:
Mv faith looks up to Thee,
Thou Lamb of Calvary,
Saviour divine!
Now hear me while I pray;
Take all my guilt away;
Oh! let me from this day
Be wholly Thine!

May Thy rich grace impart
Strength to my fainting heart,
My zeal inspire!
As Thou hast died for me,
Oh! may my love to Thee
Pure, warm, and changeless be,
A living fire!

When life's dark maze I tread,
And griefs around me spread,
Be Thou my Guide!
Bid darkness turn to day,
Wipe sorrow''s tears away,
Nor let me ever stray
From Thee aside.

When ends life's transient dream,
When death's cold sullen stream
Shall o'er me roll;
Blest Saviour! then in love
Distrust and fear remove,
O bear me safe above,
Aransomed soul!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O God, our help in ages past
verses:
O God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Oar shelter from the stormy blast,
And our eternal home
Beneath tho shadow of Thy throne
Thy saints have dwelt secure;
Sufficient is Thine arm alone,
And our defence is sure.

Before the hills in order stood,
Or earth received her frame,
From everlasting Thou art God,
To endless years the same.
A thousand ages in Thy sight
Are like an evening gone;
As short the watch that ends the night
Before the rising sun.

Time, like an overflowing stream,
Bears all its sons away:
They fly forgotten, as a dream
Dies at the opening day.
JF Our God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Be Thou our guard while troubles last,
And our eternal home.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Saviovg! is Thy promise fled
verses:
O Saviovg! is Thy promise fled
Nor longer might Thy grace endure
To heal the sick, and raise the dead,
And preach the Gospel to the poor

Come! JxEsvs, come! return in;
With brighter beam Thy servants bless,
Who long to feel Thy perfect reign,
And share Thy kingdom's happiness.

A feeble race, by passion driven,
In darkness and in doubt we roam,
And lift our anxious eyes to heaven,
Our hope, our harbour, and our home.

Yet, mid the wild and wintry gale,
When death rides darkly o'er the sea,
And strength and earthly daring fail,
Our prayers, REDEEMER, rest on Thee.

Come! Jesus, come! and as of yore
The Prophet went to clear Thy way,
A harbinger Thy feet before,
A dawning to Thy brighter day

So now may grace, with heavenly shower,
Onur stony hearts for truth prepare
Sow in our minds the seed of power,
Then come, and reap Thy harvest there!

Lord, dismiss us with Thy blessing;
Fill our hearts with joy and peace
Let us each, Thy love possessing,
Triumph 'in redeeming grace:
Oh! refresh us,
Trav'lling through this wilderness!

Thanks we give and adoration
For Thy Gospel's joyful sound
May the fruits of Tby salvation
In our hearts and lives abound!
Ever faithful
To the truth may we be found!

So, whene'er the signal's given
Us from earth to call away,
Borne on angel's wing to heaven,
Glad the summons to obey,
May we ever
Reign with Christ in endless day!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Tay glorious work, O Cugrsr, is done
verses:
Tay glorious work, O Cugrsr, is done
The battle waged with death is won!
Thou erst didst leave Thy s y throne,
But heaven demands Thee now its own!

With clouds of splendor now arrayed,
Thou look'st on earth below Thee laid;
Now started from their distant posta,
Attend their King unnumbered hosts!

Assembled Heav'n in wonder waits!
Fly ope the everlasting gates!
God-man, amid the pealing sky,
Thou tak'st the Father's seat on high!

P O Priest, and Pleader, Fount of Peace,
That blood, which brought us blest release,
Which gushed from out Thine heart of love,
Thou liv'st to offer there above.

'Tis thence Thy Church, Thy spotless Bride,
Is ever nourished, beautified
Thy members, thence with life inspired,
Are with Thy hidden Sprrir fired.

Great Head! where'er Thou dost precede,
Thy Body thither dost Thou lead
Oh! may we never swerve nor stray,
But walk where Thou hast marked the way.

To Thee, O Jzsov, praise be giv'n,
Returned in triumph into heav'n!
The Faruer, SPrrit, we adore
Till time shall cease, for evermore!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Guortiovs things of thee are spoken
verses:
Guortiovs things of thee are spoken,
Zion, City of our God
He, Whose word cannot be broken,
Formed thee for His Own abode;
On the Rock of Ages founded,
What can shake thy sure repose
With salvation's walls surrounded,
Thou may'st smile on all thy foes

See the streams of living waters,
Springing from eternal love,
Well supply thy sons and daughters,
And all fear of want remove:
cres, Who can faint while such a river
ver flows their thirst t'assuage:
Grace, which, like the Lord, the Giver,
Never fails from age to age?

Saviour! we of Zion's city
Members through Thy grace became;
Though the world deride or pity,
We will glory in Thy Name!
Fading is the worldling's pleasure,
All his boasted pomp and show;
Solid joys and lasting treasure,
None but Zion's children know.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Wy, weary mourner, shed the ceaseless tear
verses:
Wy, weary mourner, shed the ceaseless tear?
Why bow thy soul beneath desponding fear?
Lift up thine eyes! behold the gladd'ning sight
For, crowned with golden rays of mercy bright,
Lo! Christ appears thine everlasting light.

Thou oft hast fallen, oft the Spirit grieved,
By sin enchained, of peace and joy bereaved
Though circled round by foes of fearful might,
Yet seek the Cross, however dark the night
For thee it beams with everlasting light.

Draw nigh the Bosom where the weary rest,
There hopeful lay thy heavy laden breast;
Though spotted over with a deadly blight,
Thy sius of scarlet there shall turn to white
Thy darkness merge in everlasting light.

With watchful care pursue thy lowly way
Thy strength shall now be as thy shining day
With faith thy shield the foeman boldly smite,
With triumph sure maintain the mortal fight:
Look up to Cuzist thine everlasting light.

Though tearful sorrow dimmed thy Saviour's eyes,
Yet, sorrow past, He rose above the skies:
Then stanch thy weeping, speed thy heavenward flight;
Thou soon shalt reach, beyond the, starry height,
Thy deathless crown of everlasting light.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Hoy Fatuer, great CREATOR
verses:
Hoy Fatuer, great CREATOR,
Source of mercy, love, and peace,
Look upon the Mediator,
Clothe us with His righteousness; Heavenly FATHER,
Through the Saviour, hear and bless.

Holy Jesus, Lord of Glory,
Whom angelic hosts proclaim,
While we hear Thy wondrous story,
Meet and worship in Thy Name, Dear REDEEMER,
In our hearts Thy peace proclaim.

Raise our hearts with rapture higher,
Fill them with the Saviour's love;
cres, Source of comfort,
Cheer us with the Saviour's love,

God the Lord, through every nation
Let Thy wondrous mercies shine!
In the song of Thy salvation
Every tongue and race combine! Great JEHOVAH
Form our hearts, and make them Thine.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Love divine, how sweet Thou art
verses:
O Love divine, how sweet Thou art!
When shall I find my willing heart
All taken up by Thee?
I thirst, I faint, I die to prove
The greatness of redeeming love,
The love of CuxistT to me.

Still stronger e'en than death or hell,
Its riches are unsearchable:
The first-born sons of light
Desire in vain its depths to see;
They cannot reach the mystery,
The length, the breadth, the height.

my God only knows the love of God:
Oh! that it now were shed abroad
In this poor stony heart!
For love I sigh, for love I pine:
This only portion, Lord, be mine;
Be mine this better part!

Oh! that I could for ever sit
With Mary at the Master's feet!
Be this my happy choice!
My only care, delight, and bliss,
My joy, my heaven on earth, be this,
To hear the Bridegroom's voice!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Ox! where shall rest be found
verses:
Ox! where shall rest be found,
Rest for the weary soul?
*T were vain the ocean-depths to sound,
Or pierce to either pole.

The world can never give
The bliss for which we sigh
'Tis not the whole of life, to live,
Nor all of death, to die.

Beyond this vale of tears
There is a life above,
Unmeasured by the flight of years
And all that life is love.

There is a death, whose pang
Outlasts the fleeting breath:
Oh! what eternal horrors hang
Around “ the second death

Lord God of truth and grace,
Teach us that death to shun;
Lest we be banished from Thy face,
For evermore undone.

Here would we end our quest
Cres. Alone are found in Thee
The life of perfect love, the rest
Of immortality
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Ox! 'twas a joyful sound to hear
verses:
Ox! 'twas a joyful sound to hear
Our tribes devoutly say:
Up Israel, to the temple haste,
And keep your festal day.

At Salem's courts we must appear
With our assembled pow'rs,
In strong and beauteous order ranged,
Like her united tow'rs.

Tis thither, by divine command,
The tribes of God repair,
Before His ark to celebrate
His Name with praise and prayer.

O pray we then for Salem's peace!
For they shall prosp'rous be,
Thou holy City of our God,
Who bear true love to thee.

May peace within thy sacred walls
A constant guest be found!
With plenty and prosperity
Thy palaces be crowned!

But most of all I'll seek thy good,
And ever wish thee well,
For Sion and the temple's sake,
Where God vouchsafes to dwell.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: THovu, Lord, by strictest searchhastknown If I the morning's wings could gain
verses:
THovu, Lord, by strictest searchhastknown If I the morning's wings could gain,
My rising up and lying down,
My secret thoughts are known to Thee,
Known long before conceived by me.

If up to heaven I take my flight,
'Tis there Thou dwell'stenthronedinlight; If mischief lurks in any part;
Or dive to hell's infernal plains,
"Tis there Almighty vengeance reigns.

And 4y beyond the western main,
Thy swifter band wonld first arrive,
And there arrest Thy fugitive.

Or shonid I try to shun Thy sight
Beneath the sable wings of night;
One glance from Thee, one piercing ray,
Would kindle darkness into day.

Correct me where I go astray,
And guide me in Thy perfect way.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Jesus, ever present
verses:
O Jesus, ever present,
O SHEPHERD, ever kind,
Thy very name is music
To ear, and heart, and mind.

It woke my wondering childhood
To muse on things above;
It drew my harder manhood
With cords of mighty love.

How oft to sure destruction
My feet had gone astray,
Wert Thou not, patient SHEPRERD,
The Guardian of my way!

How oft in darkness fallen,
And wounded sore by sin,
Thy Hand has gently raised me,
And healing balms poured in!

O SHEPHERD good! I follow
Wherever Thou wilt lead:
No matter where the pasture,
With Thee at hand to feed.

Thy Voice, in life so mighty,
In death shall make me bold:
O bring my ransomed spirit
To Thine eternal fold
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Tov art the Way: to Thee alone
verses:
Tov art the Way: to Thee alone
From sin and death we flee
And he, who would the Father seek,
Must seek Him, Lord, by Thee.

Thou art the Truth: Thy word alone
Sound wisdom can impart;
Thou only canst inform the mind,
And purify the heart.

Thou art the Life: the rending tomb
Proclaims Thy conqu'ring arm;
And those, who put their trust in Thee,
Nor death nor hell shall harm.

Thou art the Way, the Truth, the Life;
Grant us that Way to know,
That truth to keep, that Life to win,
Whose joys eternal flow.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: YE servants of the Lord
verses:
YE servants of the Lord,
Each in his office wait,
Observant of His heavenly word,
And watchful at His gate.

Let all your lamps be bright,
And trim the golden flame
Gird up your loins as in His sight,
For awful is His name.

The banquet Christ shall spread
With His Own royal hand,
And raise that faithful servant's head
Amidst th' angelic band.

Watch! 'tis your Lord's command;
And while we speak He's near:
Mark the first signal of His hand,
And ready all appear.

O happy servant he,
In such a posture found!
He shall His Lord with rapture see
And be with honour crowned.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Fount of mercy, God of love
verses:
O Fount of mercy, God of love!
How rich Thy bounties are!
The rolling seasons, as they move,
Proclaim Thy constant care.

When 'neath the bosom cf the earth
The sower hid the grain,
Thy goodness marked its secret birth,
And sent the early rain.

These various mercies from above
Matured the swelling grain;
A yellow harvest crowns Thy love,
And plenty fills the plain.

Seed-time and harvest, Lord, alone
Thou dost on man bestow
Then let him not forget to own
From Whom his blessings flow t

O Fount of love! our praise is Thine;
To Thee our songs we'll raise
And all created Nature join,
In sweet harmonious praise.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: JS Praise to God! immortal praise
verses:
JS Praise to God! immortal praise
Praise the love that crowns our days!
Bounteous Source of every joy,
Let Thy praise our tongues employ

For the blessings of the field,
For the stores the gardens yield,
For the fruits with melting juice,
Grateful gifts for mortal use;

All that Spring with bounteous hand
Scatters o'er the smiling land;
All that lib'ral Autumn pours,
Rich in her o'erflowing stores:

These to Thee, O God, we owe,
Source whence all our blessings flow
And for these our souls shall raise
Grateful vows and solemn praise.

Yet to Thee my soul should raise
Grateful vows and solemn praise;
Then, when every blessing's flown,
Love Thee for Thyself alone!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Lord of harvest! once again
verses:
O Lord of harvest! once again
We thank Thee for the ripened grain
For crops safe carried, sent to cheer
Thy servants through another year;
For all sweet holy thoughts supplied
By seed-time, and by harvest-tide.

The bare dead grain, in autumn sown,
Its robe of vernal green puts on;
Glad from its wintry grave it springs,
Fresh garnished by the Kine of kings:
80, Lord, to those, who sleep in Thee,
Shall new and glorious bodies be.

Nor vainly of Thy Word we ask
A lesson from the reaper's task:
So shall Thine angels issue forth
The tares be burnt; and the just of earth, The sport of sun
Be gathered to their Father's store.

O Lord, our prayers be daily said,
As Thou hast taught, for daily bread;
But not alone our bodies feed,
Supply our fainting spirits' need
O Bread of Life! from day to da
Be Thou their Comfort, Food, an: not Stay!
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Comx, ye thankful people, come
verses:
Comx, ye thankful people, come!
aise the song of Harvest-home!
All is safely gathered in
Ere the winter storms begin:
God our Maker doth provide
For our wants to be supp!ied:
Come to God's own temple, come
Raise the song of Harvest-home!

All the world is God's own field,
Fruit unto His praise to yield
Wheat and tares together sown,
Unto joy or sorrow grown:
First the blade, and then the ear,
Then the full corn shall appear:
Lord of harvest, grant that we
Wholesome grain and pure may be.

For the Lord our God shall come,
And shall take His Harvest home;
From His field shall in that day
All offences purge away
Give His angels charge at last
In the fire the tares to cast;
But the fruitful ears to store
In His garner evermore.

Even so, Lord, quickly come
To Thy final Harvest-home;
Gather Thou the people in,
Free from sorrow, free from sin;
There for ever purified,
In Thy presence to abide
Come, with all Thine angels, come,
Raise the glorious Harvest-home|
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Lord of hosts, Whose glory fills
verses:
O Lord of hosts, Whose glory fills
The bounds of the eternal hills,
And yet vouchsafes, in Christian lands,
To dwell in temples made with hands.

O grant that we, who here to-day,
Rejoicing, this foundation lay,
May be in very deed Thine Own,
Built on the precious Corner-stone.

Endue the creatures with Thy grace,
That shall adorn Thy dwelling-place;
The beauty of the oak and pine,
The gold and silver, make them Thine.

To Thee they all pertain, to Thee
The treasures of the earth and sea;
And when we bring them to Thy throne,
We but present Thee with Thine Own

Both now and ever, Lord, protect
The temple of Thine Own elect;
Be Thou in them, and they in Thee,
O ever blessed Trinity
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: O Jesu, where Thy people meet
verses:
O Jesu, where Thy people meet,
They there behold Thy mercy-seat;
Where'er they seek Thee Thou art found
And where Thou art is hallowed ground

For Thou, within no walls confined,
Inhabitest the humble mind
Such ever bring Thee where they come,
And, parting, take Thee to their home.

Great SuuPHERD of Thy chosen few,
Thy former mercies here renew,
And still to wayward hearts proclaim
The sweetness of Thy saving Name.

Here may we prove the might of prayer,
To strengthen faith, and sweeten care
To teach our faint desires to rise.
And bring all heaven before our eyes.

Nor short Thine arm nor deaf Thineear:
Ocome with might and mercy down,
And make our cleansed hearts Thine
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord of hosts! to Thee we raise
verses:
Lord of hosts! to Thee we raise
Here a house of prayer and praise;
Thou Thy people's hearts prepare,
Here to meet for praise and prayer.

Let the living here be fed
With Thy Word, of the heavenly Bread
Here, in hope glory blest,
May the dead be laid to rest

Here to Thee a temple stand,
While the sea shall gird the land!
Here reveal Thy mercy sure,
While the sun and moon endure!

Hallelujah! earth and sky
To the joyfal sound reply
if Wallelujah! hence ascend
Prayer and praise till time shall end.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: t BLESSED City! Happy Salem
verses:
t BLESSED City! Happy Salem!
Peace is thine eternal name!
Fashioned in celestial regions,
Living stones have knit thy frame;
Thou art decked by waiting angels,
Like a Bride of saintly fame.

Blooming fresh, from heaven descending,
For the wedding-chimber dight,
As a fair affianced virgin,
Fitted for her Bridegroom's sight;
All thy streets and wails are blazing,
Built of gold, thrice-pure and bright.

Gleam with pearls thy sparkling portals
Open lie thy stretching shrines:
They, who for their Lord have suffered,
Whom to crush the world combines,
There, by virtue of His merits,
Every saint in glory shines,

Hammered stones of smoothest polish,
Chiselled by Divine command,
In their places are cemented
By the Builder's artful hand,
Ranged throughout thy holy structures,
There for ever will they stand.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: JS Christ is laid the sure Foundation
verses:
JS Christ is laid the sure Foundation,
Corner-stone from heavenly hands;
Firm the coupled walls uniting,
Both He links with sacred bands:
Holy Sion, thus supported,
Resting on Him ever stands.

Loved of God, to God devoted,
High the City doth upraise
Loudest songs of exultation,
Bursting strains of measared praise
Of Tsree in Ove her God proclaiming,
Sounding forth triumphant lays.

God of Heav'n! in this Thy temple,
When implored O be Thou nigh;
With Thy tenderest compassion,
Hearken to our prayerful cry
Send us down Thy richest blessing
Evermore, as here we lie.

Here bestow on all Thy suitors
What they crave in meek request
Ever holding fast Thy mercies,
Joined for ever with the blest;
Then Thy Paradise to enter,
There translated to Thy rest.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Thou, Whose Almighty Word
verses:
Thou, Whose Almighty Word
Chaos and darkness heard,
And took their flight
Hear us, we humbly pray,
And, where the Gospel's day
Sheds not its glorious ray,

Thou, Who didst come to bring,
On Thy redeeming wing,
Healing and sight,
eres, Health to the sick in mind,
Sight to the inly blind,
Oh! now to all mankind

Spirit of truth and love,
Life-giving, holy Dove,
Sveed forth Thy flight!
crea. Move on the waters' face,
Bearing the lamp of grace,
And in earth's darkest place

Holy and bless¢d Three,
Glorious Tarsity,
Wisdom. Love, Might!
Boundless as ocean's tide,
Rolling in fullest pride,
Through the earth far and wide,
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Fruitful let Thy sorrows be
verses:
Fruitful let Thy sorrows be;
By Thy pains and consolations,
Draw the Gentiles unto Thee ; 3
Of Thy Cross the wondrous story,
Be it to the nations told;
Let them see Thee in Thy glory,
And Thy mercy manifold.

Far and wide, though all unknowing,
Pants for Thee each mortal breast;
Human tears for Thee are flowing,
Human hearts in Thee would rest,
Thirsting, as for dews of even,
As the new-mown grass for rain,
Thee they seek, the God of heaven,
Thee, as Man, for sinners slain.

Saviour, lo! the isles are waiting,
Stretched the hand, and strained the sight,
For Thy Spirit, new creatin:
Love's pure flame and wisdom's light:
Give the word, and of the preacher
Speed the foot, and touch the tongue,
Till on earth by every creature
Glory to the Laws, be sung.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Soxprers of the Cross, arise
verses:
Soxprers of the Cross, arise!
Gird you with your armour bright!
Mighty are your enemies,
Hard the battle ye must fight.

Over a faithless, fallen world,
Raise your banner in the sky
Let it float there, wide unfurled;
Bear it onward, lift it high.

nyf "Mid the homes of want and woe,
Strangers to the living Word,
Let the Saviour's herald go,
Let the voice of hope be heard.

Where the shadows deepest lie,
Carry Truth's unsulied ray
Where are crimes of blackest dye,
There the saving Sign display.

To the weary and the worn
Tell of realms where sorrows cease;
To the outeast, and forlorn,
Speak of mercy and of peace.

Guard the helpless, seek the strayed,
Comfort troubles, banish grief
With the Spretr's sword arrayed,
Scatter sin and unbelief.

Be the banner still unfarled
Bear it bravely still abroad
Till the kingdoms of the world
Are the kingdoms of the Lord.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Aritsz, O Lord, and shine
verses:
Aritsz, O Lord, and shine,
In all Thy saving might,
And prosper each design
To spread Thy glorious light;
Let heal.ng streams of mercy flow,
That all the earth Thy truth may know.

Bring distant nations near
To sing Thy glorious praise
Let every people hear,
And learn Thy holy ways!
Reign, mighty God! assert Thy cause,
And govern by Thy righteous laws!

Put forth Thy glorious power,
That Gentiles all may see,
And earth present her store
In converts born to Thee:
God, our own God, H's Church shall bless,
And fill the earth with righteousness.

To God, the only wise,
The one immortal King,
Let hallelujahs rise
From every living thing!
of Let all that breathe, on every coast,
Praise Father, Son, and Hoty Guost!

We give Thee but Thine Own,
Whate'er the gift may be:
All that we have is Thine alone,
A trust, O Lord, for Thea,

May we Thy bounties thus
As stewards true receive,
And gladly, as Thou blessest us,
To Thee oar first-fruits give.

Ob! hearts are bruised and dead,
And homes are bare and cold;
And lambs, for whom the Shepherd bled,
Are straying from the fold!

To comfort and to bless,
To find a balm for woe,
To tend the lone and fatherless,
Is angels' work below.

The captive to release,
To God the lost to bring,
To teach the way of life and peace,—

And we believe Thy word,
Though dim our faith may be,
Whate'er for Thine we do, O Lord,
We do it unto Thee.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: God of mercy, throned on high
verses:
Young and erring travellers, we
All our dangers do not know;
Scarcely fear the stormy sea,
Hardly feel the tempest blow.

Saviour, give us faith, and Four
Hope and love on every soul:
Hope, till time ehall be no more;
Love, while endless ages roll!

JxEsv, lover of the young,
Cleanse us with Thy blood divine
Ere the tide of sin grow strong,
Save us, keep us, make us Thine!

Let us ever hear Thy voice
Ask Thy counsel day by day;
Saints and angels will rejoice,
If we walk in Wisdom's way.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: By cool Siloam's shady rill
verses:
By cool Siloam's shady rill,
How sweet the lily grows!
How sweet the breath, beneath the hill,
Of Sharon's dewy rose!

Lot such the child, whose early feet
The paths of peace have trod!
Whose secret heart, with influence

The rose, that blooms beneath the hill, In childhood, manhood, age, and death,
Must shortly fade away.

And soon, too soon, the wintry hour
Of man's maturer age
Will shake the soul with sorrow's power,
And stormy passion's rage.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord, this day Thy children meet
verses:
Lord, this day Thy children meet
In Thy courts with willing feet
Unto Thee this day they raise
Grateful hearts in hymns of praise.

Not alone the Day of rest
With Thy worship shail be blest
In our pleasure and our glee,
Lord, we would remember Thee,

Help us unto Thee to pray,
Hallowing our happy day;
From Thy Presence thus to win
Hearts all pure, and free from sin,

All our pleasures here below,
Saviour, from 'hy mercy flow:
But if earth has joys like this,
What shall be our heavenly bliss!

Make, O Lord, our childhood shine
With all lowly grace, like Thine:
Then throngh all eternit:
We shall live in Heaven with Thee.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lord, in mine agony of pain
verses:
Lord, in mine agony of pain
T turn mine eyes to Thee,
In humble trust, that as my day
My promised strength will be
Teach me to pray with Thy dear Son,
Gather, Thy will, not mine be done.”

Sleepless I pass the weary night,
And long for dawn of day;
The dawning day no respite brings,
Again for night I pray:
Thou, Lord, canst aid, and Thou alone!
Help me to say, “' Thy will be done.”

'Tis Thine, my sharpest pains to soothe,
And dry each falling tear;
cres, 'Tis Thine, by precious promises,
My fainting heart to cheer:
In patience then my race I'll run,
Still meekly pray, '* Thy will be done.”

A moment's light affliction here
On earth, bears no compare
To that eternal weizht of bliss,
With Jesus I shall share:
The cross on earth, in heaven the crownt
Farner, Thy will, not mine be done.”
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: My health was firm, my day was bright
verses:
My health was firm, my day was bright,
And I presumed 'twould ne'er be night
I fondly said within my heart,
My joy and peace shall ne'er depart.

But I forgot Thine arm was strong,
Which made my mountain stand so long;
When once Thy face began to hide,
My health was gone, my comforts died.

I cried aloud to Thee, my God:
What canst Thou profit by my blood?
Laid deep in dust, can I declare
Thy truth, or sing Thy goodness there?

O hear me, God of grace,” I said,
And bring me from among the dead:
Thy word rebuked the pains I felt,
Thy pard'ning love removed my guilt.

My groans, and tears, and forms of woe,
Are turned to joy and praises now;
I throw my sackcloth on the ground,
And ease and gladness gird me round.

My tongue, the glory of my frame,
Bhall ne'er be silent of Thy Name;
Thy praise shall sound through earth and heaven,
For sickness healed, and sins forgiven.
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Lit not thou the wailing voice
verses:
Pour not thou the bitter tear;
Heaven its book of comfort opeth,
Bids thee sorrow not, nor fear,
But as one who always hopeth;
Humbly here in faith relying,
Peacefully in Jesus dying,
Heavenly joy his face is flushing:
Why should thine with tears be gushing

They who die in Crntst, are blest:
Our's then be no thought of grieving;
Sweetly with their God they rest,
All their toils and troubles leaving
So be our's the faith that saveth,
Hope, that every trial braveth,
Love, that to the end endureth,
And, through Curisz, the crown sccureth
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Iris the Lord! behold His hand
verses:
Iris the Lord! behold His hand,
Outstretched with an afflictive rod;
Andhark! a voice goes through the land,
Be still, and know that I am God!”

Shall we, like guilty Adam, hide
In darkest shades, our darker fears?
For who His coming may abide?
Or who shall stand when He appears?

Who knows but God will hear our cries,
Turn swift destruction from our path,
Restrain His judgments, or chastise
In tender mercy, not in wrath?
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Wa krxc on the wing?d wind
verses:
Wa krxc on the wing?d wind,
Fear before Him, Death behind,
When the Lord came down in wrath,
Clouds and darkness girt His path!
Thence abroad His arrows flew,
Thick and fast they smote and slew
We in dust and ashes lay:
None could help, but all could pray.
Prayer prevailed amidst despair
God delights to answer prayer;
hymns.source: The Anglican Hymn Book (Singleton & Monk, 1st ed., 1868)

hymns.title: Jesus, Lord, we kneel before Thee
verses:
Jesus, Lord, we kneel before Thee;
Bend from heav'n Thy gracious ear!
While our waiting souls adore Thee,
Friend of helpless sinners, hear! By Thy mercy,
Oh! deliver us, good Lord!

Taught by Thine unerring Spirit,
Boldly we draw nigh to God,
Only in Thy spotless merit,
Only through Thy precious blood;
cres, By Thy mercy,
Oh! deliver us, good Lord!

From thedepthsof nature's blindness,
From the hard'ning pow'r of sin,
From all malice and unkindness,
From the pride that lurks within,
By Thy mercy,
Oh! deliver us, good Lord!

Jesus, may Thy promised blessing
Comfort to our souls afford!
May we, now Thy love possessing,
Find at last the great reward!
ores.
Oh! deliver us, good Lord!

When temptation sorely presses,
In the day of Satan's pow'r,
In our times of deep distresses,
